To say it's inspired by gothic 1 is a massive understatement. It is, however, a much more grounded world. Mechanically polished.... But I would have liked more content especially towards the endgame. 

Lackluster in the "reactivity" department, but does a good job of pretending otherwise. 

Despite a fine aesthetic, the choice of going isometric has had an impact on the immersion of the experience in comparison to its inspiration.

Despite all that I highly enjoyed it. Difficulty is right where it needs to be. Story is engaging albeit quite simple. Combat is finely tuned and high skill; it feels good, and you know it is always your fault for messing up. You're free to wander the world and run into too high level of an enemy, sit on it for two hours and eventually win. Although cheesing fights via instant healing potions is a bit of a downer later on, early in the game with only over-time heals, hits the spot right where it needs to.

I found Drova to be a very focused game, a quality rarely seem nowadays; it's content is very well made and nothing seems like pointless filler. Combat is fun, characters are interesting, and you will most of the time be rewarded for exploring the world. The beginning is challenging and you will die a lot, but part of feeling powerful in games is knowing how weak you were when you started, and Drova really delivers in that regard.

Overall an amazing indie game in a sea of pointless samey roguelites.

This is a fun RPG, with some very satisfying progression where you start off barely being able to fight rats, and gradually acquire equipment and skills to take on greater challenges.

I think the game could have done more to guide the player with the quests, I feel like I spent half the time just meandering around the massive map trying to decipher what the quest wants me to do or who to speak to. This aspect really drags out the game, coupled with the slow player movement.

In all, a good experience with fun progression, but a rather tedious amount of walking around.

Note: my playtime is inflated by leaving the game idle in the background for hours at a time, but this is still a fully-fledged 30-40 hour CRPG.  

I've never played any of the Gothic games, so I can't compare Drova to them, but I picked it up after Steam recommend it as being similar to CrossCode, and I wasn't disappointed.  There's exploration, secrets, lots and lots of tunnels, good music, challenging combat, and a handful of puzzles.  Don't be fooled by the retro graphics; the game is surprisingly sophisticated, with a full day/night cycle, weather, and an overworld that's at least as large and detailed as the classic 2D Zelda games.  

I do have a few complaints: 

* Some of the controls can be finicky, at least with a XBox One controller, in particular fishing was frustratingly difficult and it's too easy to double-dodge (which offers no real benefit over dodging once, and consumes double stamina)

* Most of the characters are kind of flat 

* Though there's plenty of gameplay tutorials, the game doesn't hold the player's hand at all when it comes to completing content.  For the most part I appreciated this, and I have only myself to blame for not consistently marking areas of interest on my map that I knew I'd need to return to later, but too many quests involve talking to obscure NPCs whose locations were unclear.  It'd also be nice if the game gave at least *some* indication of which enemies are too difficult for the player to challenge at their current level being getting one-shot and having to reload, and which of the generally indistinct NPCs has a sidequest available.  

Those are pretty minor though, I still recommend Drova without significant reservations.

Very good and well made "old school" RPG, and like other reviews say, reminiscent of Gothic/Risen series. The story telling is superb and the combat is relatively easy to get into, I just wish there was an alternate way to get into magic earlier.
Great classic RPG. good exploration, challenging combat.

Going into this game, I expected it to just be another CRPG that I would play for a week and then forget about afterwards. But it is so much more than that.

Firstly, I love Celtic and Anglo-Saxon mythology, so that alone was the driving factor for me buying this game. But the world building and writing is amazing, with all decisions having heavy consequences that affect the game in massive ways. There is a semi-morality system, where if you act like a jerk, you'll be recognized as one, but if you're a good person, you'll be recognized as one instead.

The combat is surprisingly nice and intuitive, with many differeny play styles for what kind of adventurer you want to be. I personally chose to do Daggers with high dexterity. But you can really play this game however you want, which is freeing.

This game was a massive adventure that immersed me in the land of Drova. I highly recommend it to anyone looking to sink their teeth in a good CRPG.

Great game, love the combat exploration and world building. Some quests are a bit tedious but not overwhelmingly so. Finished it once and it gripped me enough to try it again taking different routes. With so many indie games being roguelikes and incrementals these days this was for sure a breath of fresh air and a great time :))
Great active RPG with Celtic Fallout theme and fun fights

The Gothic 2D comparisons are accurate, and it is an enjoyable game. I did one playthrough at around 29 hours and had good fun. It captured the spark I was looking for, and for that, it gets a positive review.

However, I also have my critiques, specifically regarding the writing. The characters at times feel childish; a strong character is often forced into cartoonish or foolish behavior, and a serious situation often gets undercut by Disney like humor. Obviously, the pixel art and the small animations, such as characters laughing, do not help. Adding to that, is the overarching lore is just not very captivating and does not create any kind of difficult moral dilemma. The consequences are one sided.

This leads to me not caring about or feeling empathy for anyone in Drova as they do not feel real, with few exception.  Animals here have the bonus that they can not talk and as such you do care about them more, shoutout to Cay the Pig, which, in regard to the story (spoilers: Essentially a Princess Mononoke-like situation, just more morally simple, there is a clearly a right choice to be made), is unintentionally fitting.

Still, if they tried to be inspired by Gothic, then this is the greatest miss, as the believable asshole characters in Gothic were one of the things that made its worldbuilding so great.

I'm 40 hours in this game and I still haven't completed the first chapter, I have just been running around completing side quests here and there, I bought the game at full price and I already feel like I got my money's worth out of just this.

It's style is very reminiscent of old games and that you don't need to have the latest graphics to make something beautiful. The combat that's been done is pretty cool too and it felt moderately challenging? I've been running in leather armor through the entire of chapter 1 and it left me with that impression. I don't know how much having better armor changes things but as it stands I adored it. There is a bit of variety in weapons too, not a huge one but enough that each weapon has it's own feel and playstyle, my favorite so far has been the spear and the daggers but there's also axes, bows, swords and boards too. I also heard that later in game you get access to proper magic which leaves my spellsword urges tingling.

The story ain't half bad too, you've got two big factions with different ideologies and some other smaller ones, I don't know if you can join those, but so far the game gave me the choice to join one of the big factions. Both of them have some lovable characters and I reckon it just depends to which you feel more like joining with.

There is some bad apples here and there, I think my biggest letdown was when I figured out that enemies don't respawn, I know that it's because that how the game has been balanced and running around seeing your past hefty work is nice but eventually you'll run out of things to kill, which is somewhat dissapointing as it leaves some skills you pick eventually be worth less and less overtime (looking at you hunting), but this can most likely fixed by mods I believe?

The other being that you can't do pure mage from the very start as you get instead consumable scrolls, granted though magic packs quite a punch and looks cool as fuck.

Overall i'd give this game a solid 8/10, Consider getting this if you feel like playing something a bit more old school

A great isometric and thought-provoking RPG I wasn't expecting to enjoy as much as I did. It's got a solid story, charm, humor, RPG elements, and tough combat. I didn't love running from place to place constantly, but you eventually unlock "fast travel" and the map is generally manageable. Just don't go far off the beaten path and expect to always survive!

You can craft and upgrade your weapons, armor, and stats without being overwhelmed by skill trees. I wish crafting had been more fleshed out and complex. Overall, Drova is a great RPG romp that had me chuckling, being a wise-ass, and emotionally torn up from story-driven consequences I couldn't avoid.
Just finished this @32 hours. Really excellent RPG. Gorgeous pixel art, great story, lots of character options. Can't recommend enough. Great job Just2D!

I didn't expect to like this as much as I did.  I don't have a lot to add to other commenters, but if you're old enough you'll get what I'm saying when I say this feels like the natural evolution of the old Quest For Glory Sierra games.  For me its the perfect blend of systemic RPG and hand-crafted adventure gaming.  With just enough dialogue that I don't mind reading.

Fühlt sich an wie Gothic. Kann das Spiel definitiv an alle weiterempfehlen, die Gothic mochten. Zwei negative Aspekte möchte ich trotzdem ansprechen: 1. Fehlende Sprachausgabe. 2. In den späteren Akten läuft man viel von A nach B und hat kaum noch quests, sondern nur noch Kämpfe vor sich. Das war bei Gothic auch nie anders, aber schon da waren die ersten Kapitel meist spannender. Insgesamt trotzdem ein sehr gutes Spiel.

Took me 34 hours to get through my first run. Granted, I am rather slow and I love to immerse myself in the details. This game was really fun! I enjoyed the art style and all the different secrets and weapons. At no point did the game feel "easy," neither was it unbearably difficult. I recommend it.
Wow, came out of nowhere for me and I enjoyed it greatly. Can be played as a find your own way rpg or a google it rpg with either option supporting a good time
Amazing game. Has more depth, quests, and choices than I could have expected. Amazing open world concept with intuitive systems that make exploration fun and rewarding.

I only have a couple of hours at the time of this review, and wow, I'm just perplexed at the amount of detail and love the developers put into this game. Everything you do in this game has ramifications that you must be willing to deal with. 
I was skeptical about the combat, but it very pleasantly surprised me, EVERYTHING you do has meaning, and there are lots of deep mechanics. 

This game really shows how low the AAA gaming industry has sunk. 

If you're thinking about buying this game, do yourself a favor and DO IT, the devs deserve all the support they can get.
Deceivingly good, crazy how a pixel graphic game can be so immersive.
Absolutely fantastic story and world building. The mechanics are also quite nice and voice acting sublime.

Fantastic game. I love the pixel style which works really well. A great story with humor and tense. Love the way how you control the character and that you can choose different paths.

For me as someone who completely lost the motivation to play a game longer than 30 minutes this brought me back to some 2 to 3 hour sessions 🙂
There's a bit of a learning curve and you get your butt handed to you for a bit at the start but it gets real fun real fast! Super addictive though, really feels like an old rpg.

Gothic 2 was one of my favorite games growing up. I never thought I'd get that feeling again. Drova finally scratched that itch for me. This is a beautifully crafted game with incredible attention to detail. Thank you for this experience! Now I only hope we'll get to see more in the future
Really fun and harkens back to old school RPGs.  The pixel graphics are charming and the exploration has me hooked!

buyed drova for full price and i can 100% recommend this game, even if iam still in act 1.
This is a MUST HAVE for every gothic-series fan, its heavily inspired by it and affects my opinion on top, in a positiv way. ( you may even find some easter eggs ;) )

I can also recommend this game experience to everyone else, who likes good character and story writing.
The combat is very fun to play.
The choices you make really matters and it has impact to the world.
Rough enviroment so prepare to die a lot of times if you take the wrong turn. Its open world and you can go everywhere from the beginning.
Amazing Artstyle.

Loved it. Amazing game. Going from a zero to hero felt satisfying. At the beginning you have no skills and are using tree branches as weapons. But building up your character by training with different teachers and becoming a BAMF was so rewarding.
Took me about 41 hours to finish this game on the hardest difficulty with completing probably 90+% of the content. Absolutely worth it.
Incredibly well made RPG. The atmosphere, writing, and combat were all superb and came together to create something enthralling. Excited to see what comes next from this studio.
If you're a fan of Gothic, you'll love this game. It draws from the Gothic series, but it's also unique with its own world and characters. It's one of the best RPGs I've played in years.
Stumbled upon this game, it's a gem. Well designed RPG. Simple but deep enough to hold my attention. I am actually enjoying this more than I enjoy most AAA titles these days.

It's been ages since I truly enjoyed playing a game.
quests - easy to follow
combat - simple but hard
breath of fresh air
fight, explore, loot, craft, play more
Great game with a smart power crawl, but there are no quest markers which can get annoying at times. Would rec this to any RPG fan

A very good game that I enjoyed multiple playthroughs of.  A charming and gritty world with many characters to meet and foes to fight.  Satisfying combat and character progression make you grow from a filthy nobody into a mighty hero which is satisfying and yet the late game encounters feel difficult enough to put you through your paces.  My only gripe is that magic and leveling the mind attribute that goes along with it isn't unlocked until about halfway through, so if you want to play a pure magic master you will be weak as a kitten until getting access to your powers, but if you held out your points for it, you will then become powerful as a divinity.  (Probably not recommended for your first playthrough though.)  Pick up this gem of a game and have some fun!

Absolutely love it!

Please do a second part!
Some improvements in graphics (better textures and some more detail), voice acting and some sort of mage class and i would totally be willing to pay full price :)

Simply put: Fantastic game. I have over 600 games in my Steam library plus all the stuff on the other clients like Epic, Gog, Xbox etc.  Few titles hook me like Drova did. Simple but very effective mechanics, good writing and a lovely world to explore. The size is perfect and you can spot the love of the developer all over the place. If you speak german, you can find many little fun details.
Amazing game! As a long-time Gothic fan and a programmer fantasizing about making my own game, this is pretty close to what I consider my dream game.
Combat is punishing but fun. Great story so far. Progression feels solid.

Delightful gem of a game to play which is told through Gothic lens. Having the freedom to explore so much or so little is always something I seek out in RPGs and Drova delivered on that quite well. Having tough challenges present that are insanely difficult early on, but plausible to do is something I love. A world set and one that does not "mold" around the PCs power level. Puzzles in the game weren't  too difficult, but just enough that got you scratching your head. 

The game is methodical. The combat is real time, but often needing to be taken slowly. To someone like me I adore it as it returns to roots where every encounter is deadly. However, its understandable that not everyone enjoys that kind of gameplay. Similarly there are no map markers and the quests themselves does not have much in the way of handholding.

Had a great time with this game. It's a complete experience. It's challenging, densely packed with content, heavily rewards exploration, and doesn't outstay its welcome. It has two story paths dependent on which faction you decide to join. My Nemeton playthrough took about 34 hours. I did most of the quests and explored intently for endgame gear. The sense of progression from the start of the game to the end is tremendous: in the beginning, you're searching every nook and cranny for supplies, cautiously fighting water rats and baby spriggans. By the end you can become a godlike entity, given pause by only the most challenging of encounters.

My only issues were that the dialogue sometimes felt a little off tonally (e.g. calling beer "brewskis"), and I think a third option for the main quest to side with the Refuge druids who live in harmony with the divinities would've been an excellent addition. 

Overall, highly rate this game and definitely recommend it to fans of old school ARPGs.

You like Gothic series especially first and second installment? This game is for you 100% and even if you never played them Drova is a very solid game and i highly recommend for anyone to give it a shot.

If you like to explore, to wander in the mist, then this is your game.
You have to play clever, beast and plants don't respawn, some puzzles will be hard.
Best equipement is well hiden, also most of the magic is cast by scrolls and they are quite expensive.
The narrative is lovely and you can pet cats and other animals.

Playing this game was an amazing experience, the world of Drova is great and I recommend everyone to play this game.
I devoured the whole game from start to finish, enjoying the detailed little details, all the puzzles, the funny comments from npcs, the challenging matches with enemies.
Playing this game made me feel like a little kid discovering the world of video games, this whole Drova project was a great success, and I want to thank the developers and everyone else who worked on this game! 

(This game can be quite challenging and nerve-wracking in places, but over time your character can overcome these challenges and fight his way through every enemy in his path.
Reminds me of the game "Gothic", > from zero to hero, gameplay)

Interesting gameworld.
Satisfying gameplay.
Almost everything is accessible from the beginning, but you're too weak to engage with much of it. As you level up and get better gear, more possibilities open up. None of the enemies level up with you, which gives you a satisfying feeling of power as you stomp the enemies that gave you trouble in the beginning, and can tangle with enemies that seemed impossible at the start.
the visuals are stunning and gameplay is smooth. i had a harder time getting immersed in the writing and clunky sound design.
gothic I in another setting with gameboy graphics, an interesting mana mechanic and actually fun boss fights

Great value for an open-world RPG! Drova: [i] Foreskin [/i] is rich in detail, few roadblocks will hinder exploration but it definitely feels like 90% of the map is accessible from the start. The world-building is intriguing, filled with vague puzzles and fun quests. It has great pixel animation with atmospheric sound design, exploring caves can be eerily immersive. While the map functions like a literal plain map. 

I played primarily before the Insane patch (pre-1.2.3.), where slain enemies appeared to be in a peaceful slumber. While it didn’t break immersion, the post-patch updates improved their sprites to look more decayed. Small enhancements like this just shows quality.

I will definitely dive back in once they released a major patch or a Game of the Year Edition.

As Drivanius said, Bygone’s history is another story, hopefully it’s a tease from Just2D. 🙂
Fantastic game, just buy it.  If this looks a bit like your thing, just get it.. its great.
This grimdarkish RPG plays like the classics from the olde days. Don't sleep on this one!
A better Gothic-like game than anything Piranha Bytes have developed in the last two decades.
Amazing arpg! Never played Gothic games but to me Drova feels like a mix of Diablo, Fallout 1 & 2 & Stardew Valley!
Games like this are undeniable proof that the people who claim that gaming is dead simply aren't playing the right games. Get it, play it. It's great.

This was not what I was expecting from an ARPG as most of them tend to focus on repetitive hack/slash/loot.  
Instead this offers a very rich story with tons of unique characters, well written dialog and a changing world to explore.  The combat keeps you on your toes as most of the enemies can kill you easily until you learn their timings.  While you do get more powerful most of your experience comes not from killing the same enemies but from exploring and completing quests.  You will also have to face difficult choices on who to help and then face the often dire consequences!

I did not care for this game. I felt like I was constantly running into fights I wasn't levelled or geared for. I was following along the story and not making detours into high-level areas. The power scale in the early game is either 'this is very easy' or 'you are completely outmatched'. I rallied two miners to attack a corrupt guard and the three of us weren't able to take him down. Not heroic or fun for me.
Masterpiece pixelart and great story!
a good adventure, challenging and rewarding

Every time you think you know how big, deep, or surprising Drova will be, another layer gets peeled back. Deeply satisfying, charming, weird, and downright fun. I genuinely hope these devs get to keep making games at exactly this scale, with the same clear-eyed passion and execution. Cannot recommend this enough to any fan of action-oriented RPG's.

For Nemeton!

This game reminds me of when I was a kid just discovering games back in the late 90's and early 2000's. That feeling of freshness, discovery,struggle. This game has a great story, buttload of side quests that actually feel like quests and not that boring go fetch me something and over quest. The quests have parts and they all intertwine. Your actions actually matter which makes your choices in the dialogue dynamic. The combat is nothing to be "OMG" about but it's good and there is a selection of different weapons and rarity to them. Anywho I can go on forever about the good things about this game but the main thing I loved was how long the game is. It took me 16 ish hours to get done the first chapter of the game and there are 5!.

Very strong RPG featuring Celtic legends. Good: 1. Fabolous combat system, a lot of skills, talents and abilities. 2. Quests are interesting and not trivial. 3. Open world, but there is story line. 4. Interesting choices for game ending. 5. Good crafting system, a lot of recipes. Room for improvement: a lot of arcade elements - inventory is unlimited, also unlimited potions during the battle, no companions.

I was not prepared for what this game gave me. I am glad I got the chance to experience this.

The art style and promise of an interesting-looking RPG experience was what initially drew me in. But Drova was truly an engrossing game.

It embodies that climb to greatness so well. At first, you pick your fights carefully. You scrounge for each penny. You scout out and explore, fearing you might encounter that next hurdle that seems impossible. But the sense of adventure is... it's truly what drives you to see what treasures, secrets and history might be tucked away in the ruins, caves and forests.

Then as the game goes on, you make a name for yourself. You become a hero, someone worthy of leading a legend, someone truly capable of leaving a mark on history.

For this price, it's an easy recommend.

Was brutal for me at start, think i quit playing after 20 minutes or so 3 times but i finally pushed through some and got the map which helps a ton.  Enjoying the game a lot, playing on hard and its definately challenging...expect it to be hard or go easier diff but not sure what they are like didnt try those.
Great game with great story. I really enjoyed combat in this game.
If Gothic and SNES' Secret of Mana, of old school Squaresoft fame, had a beautiful, beautiful lovechild, this would be it.

This was a great game. Felt like a modern old school game (if that makes any sense). The game doesn't mess around but it rewards exploration and a careful approach that felt very rewarding. You start off being worried about so much as straying off the road, but the power creep as you find good gear builds your strength and by the end i had mastered my moveset and was tearing it up wherever i went. Went with spear/shield mostly and it felt great. The puzzles were decent and the story too. I got what i assume is the good ending and it leaves room for more without ending on a cliffhanger or anything. Highly recommended and cant wait to see where they go with this IP.

An excellent RPG in a vibrant, handcrafted, setting. Combat feels great with all the necessary components working well together.
The best part of the game is the faffing about and finding out. You will get chewed up by something pointy if you walk off the path, at any point in the entire game. But you could also get something shiny!

A rare gem of a game. I'm a huge fan of the Gothic series and this is one of the few games that truly 'gets it' and delivers similar experience. Got lost in it for a week, discovered pretty much everything there is to discover and I want more.

Overall a good game. 

Pros.
-The power progression on insane difficulty feels satisfying. 
-Exploration and doing side quests is very rewarding. 
-Combat and character building is simple but good. 

Cons.
-Story takes a nosedive in act 3 and significantly decreased my enjoyment of the game.

Bought this based on the Overwhelmingly Positive reviews and the fact it struck me as a pixel art, 2 dimensional Elden Ring. What was not originally clear to me was how much nostalgia for Gothic, a game I never played, was clearly driving the positive review train on this one. Movement and combat feels like operating a character perpetually stuck in mud. Even the dodge mechanic is somehow completely unsatisfying, and a serviceable dodge mechanic is often the only ingredient needed to get me to spend at least 2 hours on an action RPG. If this truly belongs in the Action RPG category, the combat alone puts this game on par with releases 10 years older than it, or worse.

인디라고 하기엔 꽤 높은 완성도를 가진 좋은 게임입니다. 플레이한 25년 2월 시점으로는 아직 한글화가 안되어 있어 참고하셔야 할 것 같습니다. 오픈월드 RPG를 좋아하신다면 재밌게 플레이하실 수 있을 것 같습니다. 오픈 월드에서 돌아다니며 퀘스트 깨고, 아이템 파밍하고, 레벨 올려서 빌드 만들어가는 게임입니다. 성장이 재미있고, 다크소울 느낌의 스태미나 기반 회피/방어/패링 시스템이 있어 비슷한 경험을 즐길 수 있지만, 권장 난이도인 클래식 모드로 하면 그것보다는 살짝 쉬운 느낌입니다. 스킬 사용시 소모되는 마나에 해당하는 '포커스' 시스템과 우클릭하면 마우스 주변을 자세히 살펴보는 시스템이 독특해서 흥미로웠습니다. 참고하실만한 점은 4종류의 근접 무기와 2종류의 원거리 무기, 그리고 마법으로 공격 수단이 나뉘는데, 게임 디자인상 근접 무기가 거의 무조건 메인이 될 수밖에 없고, 마법이나 원거리 무기는 보조 수단에 불과한 느낌이 있습니다. 억지로 활이나 마법 빌드를 할라면 할 수 있겠지만, 게임 디자인 자체가 그걸 염두에 둔 느낌은 아닙니다.

좋은 게임이었지만 인디 게임으로서의 한계도 많이 보였었는데, 가장 첫번째로 네비게이팅이 극도로 불편합니다. 지도는 불친절해서 길인줄 알고 갔다가 아니어서 한참을 빙 돌아서 가야하는 경우가 부지기수고 (사실 이것때문에 단순히 길 찾아 해매기만 1시간 넘게 할 때도 있습니다.) 원하는 NPC를 찾는것도 노가다로 시간이 많이 소모됩니다. 길을 헤매느라 답답한 시간이 꽤 있는 점 염두해두셔야 할 것 같습니다. 그래서 저는 원래는 공략을 잘 안보는데 이 게임에서 길 찾는데에는 봤었습니다. 자신만의 규칙을 세워서 공략을 활용하시는 것 추천합니다.

또 유적에서 종종 퍼즐을 한 두개쯤 클리어하고 나면 다음 퍼즐에서 꽉 막히는 경우가 있습니다. 그래서 도저히 모르겠어서 공략을 찾아보고 나면 그냥 막히는게 맞고 메인 스토리 깨다보면 스토리상 깨지는 거라는 경우가 꽤 있었습니다. (...) 이런 문제가 계속 되다보니 퍼즐에 대한 신뢰를 잃게 되어서 나중엔 실제로 풀 수 있는 퍼즐임에도 일단 개발자를 의심하게 되는 경우가 생깁니다. (ㅋㅋ) 스토리상 막혀있어야만 하는 퍼즐이라면, 애초에 접근 자체를 불가능하게 했어야 하지 않나 싶습니다.

결론은 너무 불친절하고 직관적이지 못한 부분들이 많아서 가끔 공략을 참고해야 했긴 하지만 돈이 아깝지는 않은 좋은 게임이었습니다. 굳.

So just a few things i dislike:
- After each stage you have to repair a few things. But the game tells you exactly how many things. There is no "i hope i found everything." You diagnose until the list is complete then you replace the parts in the "replace broken parts" list. After the race back in your garage you dont even have to diagnose the parts. all broken parts are pre-diagnosed for you. 

- There is no real "preparing" for a race. The game tells you which setup changes to make, which parts to fit, which tires to mount. Its a checklist game. you are not a mechanic, you are the mechanics low wage worker who is doing the requested work.

- Part wear has zero influence. Every part is a 1/0 condition. Its either good enough to be raced or its not. In the beginning i took half the engine apart after each race to make sure i replace parts that are worn out a bit more than i liked (around 60-70%). But since i got the dyno upgrade i realised that there is no "car condition". the engine has exactly the same power as out of the factory - or it doesnt run because one part is too low. Servicing your car is a waste of time, you only replace broken parts. Cant confirm with tires and brakes - but at least it didnt feel like the race times improved when replacing brakes and tires before the game considers them "broken".

- speaking of parts: you can repair some parts, and some you cant. I like this idea. Especially during a rally event we all know those pictures of taped together cars. Not in this game. Repairing makes a part factory new. So the only gameplay element in this is one additional minigame and random parts being paid to repair and others not. Which parts can be repaired is very random, too. not related to real life.
Oh and if you cant repair a broken part in the repair session between stages: dont worry, there is a Tardis somwhere near you where you can simple get every single part of your car, including body panels, windows, engine parts. No need to prepare for a rally by buying parts you expect you might need to replace. 
Unless its a part you didnt bring: i didnt read properly and had to change from wet gravel to wet tarmac but i only brought dry tarmac tires. So the tardis of course can just produce more dry tarmac tyres out of thin air, but getting wet tarmac tires? Nope.

I didnt make it to higher class cars, i just bought a C class and tuned it to be B class, but i dont expect there to be much more depth.

The excitment of a time running while you repair a car wears off pretty quick and after this, its just a copy of CMS2021 - but fails to even achieve CMS2018 levels.

Skip for now, maybe come back in a year or so.
Oh and the AI artwork slop others already mentioned is really wierd and doesnt paint the developers in the best light. Just pay an artist if you wnt artwork in your game. If you think its not important enough to pay someone then leave it out of the game.

There is a big BUT in this review.......
Yes I would recommend it but there is definitely some misleading marketing happening.

THE GOOD:
This is a super easy to use, 3D mapping software with a very intuitive user interface, easy control system, and is over all pleasant to create with. Out of the box you have numerous options that allow you to build any map you like in nearly any setting you like. 

The software also comes with an export feature with allows you to export the map out of Dungeon Alchemist and into the more popular, if not many of the online VTT systems like Foundry VTT and Roll20. 

BUT BUT BUT BUT BUT

THE BAD: 
For all the power this software has, it cannot export 3D maps, meaning you can look at your amazing 3D map all you want in the Dungeon Alchemist software, but don't expect to get it out. Exports will 100% in 2D. I don't know how complex it would be to do this but for all this software does and all this amazing marketing footage....your 3D map is essentially stuck. 

I spoke to one of their Discord mods who said that some people do things with the 3D images to make handouts and other have used the interface as a VTT...but when you consider all of the automation and optimization in a platform like Foundry VTT offers, there is no way I would ever sacrifice all of that just to have a 3D environment. 

HOWEVER.........BACK TO THE GOOD NEWS

Exporting your 3D map into a 2D format does still save you tons of time as the 2D export comes with well placed wall and doors and it all setup for lighting. With the Dungeon Alchemist software having a much smoother and versatile interface then trying to build a map into Foundry VTT, this is still worth the price. 

TLDR: 
I like the software but the the marketing is very misleading. You cannot export 3D maps out of Dungeon Alchemist and all the hype about what it can do in their videos and Steam advertisement is locked to the software itself. The export feature only exports 2D maps.

Blood West is a STALKER-like FPS, with a light Immersive Sim bent.

It's a fun, heart-pounding time. But some structural elements bring it down, and it is by no means for everyone.

Combat is slow and deadly. Reload times are painfully long. The game STRONGLY incentives stealthy takedowns with silent weapons like melee and bows. The game introduces a "stealth bar" that fills up to show how alert an enemy is. Nothing ground-breaking, but by being very forth-coming with the stealth mechanics, the player is empowered to make much more informed decisions about movement and positioning than your average stealth game. 

Combat itself is satisfying and crunchy, but the checkpoint system is frustrating and makes me not want to engage with the enemy at all. Basically, you have no quick-saves and quick-loads. You die, and you're sent back to the checkpoint, of which there is usually a single one, sometimes a LONG walk back to where you were. Additionally, you are not reverted to your last save, you respawn, having used up your limited ammo and potions. While, thankfully, only some monsters respawn when you die, this makes death feel like a massive set back, and makes it foolish to use any of your consumables or ammunition, since they just get flushed away forever.

Making death EVEN MORE punishing is a debuff that you get when you die. These range from, pretty small and forgettable, to big deals like a big cut to your stamina or health. The same debuff can get applied three times, where only THEN are you able to take on a quest to get rid of it.

I'm explaining all this not because I think it makes the game terrible, but because I know a lot of people would absolutely hate these punishments. But if you're a glutton for punishment, and the idea of a STALKER western with big open levels and exploration appeals to you, you'll probably have a great time. Just be aware this game likes to be a jerk to the player, and I could handle the antagonistic design for the first two episodes, but ended up tapping out in the third, as the game introduced some more and more tricky enemies

Blood West is a fun stealth/action shooter with a fun western meets Cthulu vibe. Both stealth and run-and-gun are options, exploration is pretty free-form, and once I figured out that chicken heads let you teleport between camps without reviving enemies, it became a lot less tedious to explore.

The only downside is that the game starts to outstay its welcome a little bit - Act 2 and 3 dragged on a bit more than I would have liked, but it was still a solid 20-25 hour experience.

Blood West absolutely nails its atmosphere. It gives you that eerie, "You might think you're alone… but you're definitely not" feeling. Every corner of this cursed land feels haunted, and the game makes sure you never feel safe.

As an immersive sim, you're free to play however you want. I chose the stealthy approach—just me and my trusty axe, creeping through the dark. Combat feels deliberate, and exploration rewards you with knowledge. The game is tough, but never unfair. If you pay attention to notes and your surroundings, you'll know exactly what enemies do—who alerts others, who shoots, and who you can take down quietly.

Speaking of enemies, the Birdmen? Absolutely terrifying. Every encounter with them put me on edge. The moment I alerted one, a swarm of undead rushed me. I hesitated, unsure whether to fight or flee… and I paid the price.

There are some quirks, like being able to negate fall damage by sliding down angled surfaces, which gave me Fallout: New Vegas and Skyrim vibes. Nothing game-breaking, just something I noticed.

I’d wholeheartedly recommend Blood West to fans of the Wild West, cowboys, and horror. The animations are well done and surprisingly accurate. Unfortunately, I had to refund it—not because of the game itself, but because I couldn't focus on the dialogue or gameplay. That said, if you’re up for a unique, creepy Western experience, this game is absolutely worth your time.

I never thought I'd enjoy immersive sims so much, especially after playing Gloomwood, but here we are. Of course, as much as I love that game, it's still in Early Access, and I wanted more... And this is where Blood West comes in.

Blood West is a retro stealth FPS immersive sim (Thief with guns, if you will), where you are an undead cowboy, gunning down Eldritch monstrosities. Honestly, I wish we had more games like that, because Blood West is a fantastic experience, and I'm not even that big on stealth.

I absolutely enjoyed just exploring the maps, finding secret OP as balls weapons; a proper reward for those daring to explore every nook and cranny of the Barren Lands. And the enchanted weapons and gear you can buy/find all have ups and downs, fitting various play styles. The Spirit Bow, for example, is perfect for stealth, having infinite spirit arrows, at the expense of draining your health every time you fire it. And on the topic of Dead Man's Promise, I did also enjoy it, though I do feel like it was a bit too short. Some of the new weapons were fun as hell, though I feel like the Dancing Flame revolver would have made more sense to give to our cowboy character in the base game, given that he can learn how to fan revolvers, and also obtain the cowboy hat trinket that makes revolvers much stronger. The shaman character in the DLC can't utilize revolvers as well. Still fun, though.

Overall, I absolutely loved Blood West. It's underrated as hell, and more people need to check it out. My final verdict:

[h2] [i]I want to like this game.[/i] [/h2]

As far as the gameplay is concerned, everything there is to love about Panel de Pon / Tetris Attack / Puzzle League is here.
The problem, is if you are any good at this style of gameplay, there's nothing new here. All of your garbage (regardless if it's from a combo or chain) turns into panels when the bottom row is cleared. Therefore, the game is even easier. Even worse, this has the terrible side-effect of completely removing the rhythm expert matches in this style of game have. 
The other thing, is that there are high-level mechanics in PdP/TA/PL that are simply [i]not[/i] possible here. Frame-perfect switching to keep a chain going? Forget about it.

The story mode is nice, it's a puzzle game. I'm not expecting anything groundbreaking, it does what it needs to. However, once you've done that and Versus. That's it. That's the game. Puzzle mode? Line clear? Nowhere to be found. Flipon is $4 and has a puzzle mode. Regardless of price point, missing core mainstays of the genre like this is inexcusable.

It kills me to say this but, grab this while it's on sale. There's a fun couple of hours to be had here for sure if you're new to action puzzle games. However, there's not enough content here for experts and the mechanical changes to core gameplay fundementals take what should be an exciting back and forth and turn it into a speedrun of the boring kind.

Let me be clear: I don't recommend this game in its current state. If there are future updates with story developments and gameplay mechanics I would happily recommend it.

As of right now, I downloaded it the day of release and finished the story in 88 minutes. And the story felt primarily like a pro-longed tutorial where I was learning to swap better and faster, and was being introduced to characters. Mind you, I think the characters are neat (personally would've liked some more mlm rep but that's at the bottom of the barrel of issues), and some of them I was really interested in learning more about. I even was developing some theories to how the story would continue as you went forward, and thinking about how I would write them up to see if I got any correct in the long run...

But the long run never happened. The story was less than 10 versus battles against NPCs who you (the player) just meet for the first time and get a TL;DR of their personality and story. Mind you sometimes that's fine...so long as it would be expanded upon at a later point in the story. (For example, we just found out in this story that [spoiler] Kannon was an Angel, despite us (the character) knowing him for quite some time and him literally looking nothing like the rest of the people in the town and having ACTUAL ANGELIC WINGS [/spoiler]. Facts or information that's given to us isn't given any sense to breathe - its all swapping, some light humor, and then back to swapping. 

I wanted to like this game, hell, I wanted to LOVE this game. I have had it on my wishlist since I was told of this during an Indie Developer E3 Conference in like 2022. I was so excited when I got the notification on my phone that this game finally dropped and I would be able to play. I paid, downloaded it, and was so hyped...for nothing.

I guess I can go back and romance a few options right now, but I don't see a need to do that? The story is done, what more will I learn from these people who aren't going to impact the world around us? If the spirits need swapping are still invading the town, then why are we focusing on dating? Why not get a fuller force to get this completed?

Like I said, if there are future updates with story developments and gameplay mechanics I would happily recommend it to anyone who wants some good vibes and good representation. The music is nice and fitting, the gameplay is smooth and not hard to pick up, and the characters can be interesting and fun to interact with. But it feels like the substance to this game right now is very little and I don't have a desire to go back to it until something else or more gets added.

This game is exactly what it says on the tin: [b] It's a game of LoFi chill beats to match 3 to.[/b]

I really adore the overall [b]aesthetic[/b] and ✨[b]vibe[/b]✨ of this game and am very happy to have a match 3 game in my library that doesn't look like poop. (Also, it plays smoothly on the Steam Deck!)

The main story plays a little bit like a tutorial, and so it's recommended to play, but also it's fairly quick and entirely optional, for anyone who isn't all that interested in dialogue-based story games. 

Once you're done with the main story (solid 60 minutes or so), you know everything you need to know to play Endless Mode or Versus Matches in whatever speed and difficulty setting you like. (Or you skip the tutorial/story mode completely and just figure things out on your own. It's not exactly rocket science.)

If you [i]are[/i] into the story bits, you get to hang out with, learn more about and even romance the characters; you also collect some furniture to design your room, if that tickles your fancy, and play versus matches against the other characters from within story mode. 

There doesn't seem to be huge overarching story, which, to me, is perfectly on brand with a [i]chill[/i] game. I find huge story portions that I need to get through to unlock new content a little overwhelming sometimes. In this game, the story really is in the characters and their relationships with each other. Oh, and obviously the game is very 🏳️‍🌈LGBTQIA+ friendly and body positive, which I'm very much here for.

I'd recommend this game to anyone who thinks that [b]chill beats, pastel colours and match 3 mechanics[/b] sounds like an enticing combo.

The puzzle mechanics are perfect, I can't really say much more on that. It's exactly what you would want. Big fan of the ability to force lines up on my own side so I can attack faster.

That said, where this game shines is the writing.

At time of writing I'm at just under 5 hours, beat the story in a bit less than 2 and that's with messing around. The rest? Post game conversations with other characters and more game play.

If you want to focus on just battling, you can. There is an endless and versus mode for that. Me? I want the conversations, the story, the relationships.

The story is fully voiced, and all major events in the post story content are voiced! The side stories are wonderful and charming! The art is spectacular! You can feel how much care went into ever bit of design.

Only real complaints is there are some brutal typos in the post story stuff that can get confusing. The word corner at one point was typed "cofrmer." So, I would just really like to see some proofreading done for an update, but it's relatively minor!

Anyway, TLDR: at 16 bucks, it's a steal. At full price, it's a great price for it if you enjoy relaxing to a matching puzzle game and aren't after stressing out (though I didn't try the two higher difficulties!) and want a ton of LGBTQ representation and some wonderful personalities along the way. If you're trying to get this STRICTLY for a puzzle match game, it may not be for you. If you're after a 50/50 visual novel/puzzle match game though, Yeah, it's worth your time!

P.S. If I never get to see 5HAG VISION I'mma riot!

Been waiting years for this game, and it’s just what I’ve been hoping it would be. I love the characters, the gameplay feels good, the vibes are relaxing as all hell, and I can’t wait to spend more time swappin’ spirits.

Overall I think this is a super refreshing take on Panel de Pon gameplay with great art, music, presentation, and overall vibes. The story mode feels like it's about 80% visual novel segments, and 20% puzzle gameplay. Recommend if you like puzzle/match-3 games at any level, or if you enjoy cute queer vibes.

The world is colorful and is infused with culture, which feels appreciated since there's not a lot of games out there that have this vibe. The character designs are also great, with Mo and Pookie standing out to me in particular. The writing is great, and the characters feel like they have an actual history behind them outside of the main plot of the story. There were a couple of typos and misspellings, but it's nothing that can't be fixed with a quick patch.

The spell mechanics and the changes to how garbage is cleared are both refreshing and make the "puzzle game" parts easier to get into. Spells can set up really cool stuff and add new kinds of patterns to look out for which are a welcome addition to a classic type of puzzle game. Freezing as a mechanic is interesting, but it can be hard to visually identify what type of block is frozen so it's hard to clear and unfreeze; not sure if the visual noise is also intended as part of the mechanic but it makes counterplay harder as a result.

If you're used to classic Panel de Pon, you might find the controls a bit "squidgy", especially when trying to skill chain by moving blocks underneath falling blocks. Also while clearing garbage, it seems like it's not possible to move blocks into the space where the initial clear was made to set up garbage chains, which is harder to deal with.

The "panic" animation that the blocks do is also a bit too intense for me, and makes it a bit harder to see what's going on at crucial moments as your stack rockets up to the top of the screen.

Overall, I really enjoyed the art style, music, writing, presentation, and the game design - basically all of the game! With a bit more polish I think this could be even better, but I'd still recommend playing it now anyway. Looking forward to seeing what this studio does next!

All in all, this is a super chill and fun game with the option to crank it up with the max difficulty actually being a real challenge for those who want that.

It's a fine enough game, just not for me. The soundtrack and some of the characters are cool, but I keep having this feeling of "there's something missing" that I can't get immersed. I wish Steam had a neutral recommendation, because the following issues keep rubbing me the wrong way:

[list]
[*] The board itself feels very sterile. Pieces snap into place with no motion (if any at all!), and there's none of the "juice" that makes similar games like Panepon and Flipon feel joyful to play.
[*] If both players in VS have cascades going, the game starts chugging slowly to a "seconds-per-frame" thing that still keeps game logic going, which is enough to make me lose rounds regularly. Still managed to clear the main part of Story in spite of that, though.
[*] The characters themselves feel somewhat restricted in gameplay. 1P Endless [b]REQUIRES[/b] that you play Samar, so if you like Pookie or the Trio you're out of luck. It also means you don't get to experience more of the soundtrack or backgrounds in this mode.
[*] VS on the other hand... oh jeez, where do I begin. It only lets you pick one power instead of 3, and you HAVE to pick the character that goes with that power. The game also takes its sweet time between rounds, as well.
[*] No customization for keyboard controls, which feels weird with all the accessibility options this game has.
[/list]

Six years in development, countless delays and over $150,000 in funding from Kickstarter. Glowing IGN articles, numerous showcases and interviews. This game needs to be studied, in a lab, on how NOT to create a videogame, how NOT to use backer funds, and why you SHOULDN’T hide the price/release date from your audience.

Spirit Swap is a very unique title: it was delayed, over 5 times, without any communications or updates to backers. In fact: Alex “AK” Abou Karam (who does all of the game’s social media) took months, even YEARS, not responding to backers or inquiries to if the game was dead or not. Oftentimes: the tone was aggressive, rude, and condescending. One of Alex’s replies to a backer asking about the game coming out: “However, you may have noticed a genocide happening the past 10 months and my country, where my parents and entire family live, on the brink of an all out war for roughly the same time. I’m sorry our fun little match-3 dating game is delayed longer than I wished as a result. We are still working on it and will update you all as soon as possible. Despite it all we are still working.” While the war in Gaza is heartbreaking and horrific, that is NO EXCUSE to treat backers like ignorant, out-of-the-loop entitled brats.

The Game Devs of Color Expo Interview from 12/31/2021 is a treasure trove of insight to this game’s failures. It received $15K to fund a prototype, with a team of 5 people and 13 contractors. Alex brags that they paid contractors $40 minimum wage an hour…which is supposed to “not be exploitative.” Unfortunately, these wages ARE exploitative, and it’s shocking to hear that the game funds still weren’t enough to finish development.  What was the reason Alex started their company? “When we started Soft Not Weak…my big thing was uhh…I hate this industry…” A strange admission…anything else Alex? “This industry sucks A--…and I don’t want to work with anyone in it…” Oh…what else?

“My friends are the people that, you know, that are often in the park during GDC (editor’s note: this was a number of child-adults who had a screaming session to take out their rage) as opposed to listening to 435 million white guys talking about their million dollar studio…as if the reason for their success was ‘WE MADE WEAPONS BUT WITH UHH…BEUGHHHH…instead of saying ‘we had millions of dollars.’ 

Where did all of the backer funds go? It was wasted on merchandise and frivolous spending: Alex admitted in a 2022 interview with GDOC that they underestimated basic shipping rates…so their company didn’t charge shipping from backers, thought they could get the vendor to ship by weight instead of items (note: you can do it yourself to save the $1 per item charge he was furious about), and offered too much merchandise. In this interview: at least they admit that they would only do a digital release next time. This must be reassuring for the backers that are receiving a watered down game because of all that merch!

The team, in another GDOC interview, describes the visual aesthetic as “90’s hip-hop.” I don’t remember anything Missy Elliot wore looking like this…Maybe P Diddy had some digital antlers, bad outfits and cassette tapes at the mansion? Not sure, but the art is ugly and distracting. Characters also gain/lose weight at rapid rates…the artwork between scenes doesn’t match, so a slightly chubby character suddenly appears skinny during Match-3 segments. What body-negative message does this send to people?

Alex may also be committing a felony through their Soft Not Weak LLC. In the filings, no such person (Alex) exists…so either they created the LLC using their deadname (with a different last name?), or they used someone else to file it. If the former: that is probably criminal. If the latter: this is also probably criminal. The most recent filing was in 2022, years after Alex changed their identity and name…so it’s disappointing to see that laziness, or ineptitude, got in the way of accurately reflecting their true identity when forming the company. Oh well…I'm sure the state of Washington will sort this all out.

The writing is atrocious, but that’s not surprising given Dani Lalonders’ (Validate) involvement with it. The game says it’s queer, but it comes off like a bad Steven Universe episode. There are no conflicts between the characters, nor romance, nor sex…just mild flirting and only supportive intentions. Very reminiscent of Dragon Age: Veilguard, but with writing only a middle school student would enjoy. And a middle schooler shouldn’t enjoy this: various tobacco/weed references throughout the game, including a skull hookah in a tattoo parlor.

The match-3 gameplay is a failure: you cannot use a mouse (even in menus), so you need to use either a keyboard or controller. The noise that is made when you match 3 is underwhelming…like a raindrop plopping on a leaf. Wouldn’t want cool noises or shatter effects like other popular games…nah, this needs to be a low-fi CHILL vibe. It makes the gameplay boring, tiring, and a great natural sleep aid (Almost feel asleep multiple times playing this!). Don’t worry though: if the game gets too hard (it defaults to the easiest difficulty), you can pause the game, select “Win this Round” and bypass the game entirely. Do you need to take a break from the game? Going to the main menu erases all progress you’ve made when talking to someone…so expect to redo that section of the game entirely.

As another user pointed out: ANYONE that donated to charity to play the demo…well, that demo has been taken away from you. Alex thanks Jirard in the credits, multiple times, even after his involvement with the Open Hand Foundation was uncovered. It’s sad to see Soft Not Weak supporting Jirard, even after he was caught red handed.

‘Spirit Swap’ is a boring slog through one of the worst Match-3 games in decades. The writing is awful, the characters are ugly amalgamations, and the Kickstarter funds were not used appropriately. Spirit Swap hits the perfect sweet spot with plenty of puzzle action for folks who enjoy the style of classic Puzzle League paired with a very charming cast of queer characters. It's wonderful to see such a refreshing depth and breadth of personalities and identities in one cast and it is clear that each character was crafted with love and care, especially they're wonderfully unique and vibrant character designs. The dialogue and narration do a good job at balancing out humor and sincerity, and the voice cast add such great depth to their roles, especially Jay Taylor in the lead role as Samar. 

All this is said after I've only just completed the main story mode so I'm curious to explore the epilogue and everything that comes after. I'm looking forward to exploring the romance options for sure! 

The gameplay itself is quick and snappy, replicating the original Puzzle League experience, but also adding in its own touches with the different spell abilities. Being able to mix and match your spell set helps to craft your own playstyle, which is a welcome innovation. As the title says, the music by meltycanon provides the perfect background as you snap up combos and multi-matches. 

All in all, Spirit Swap is a delightful indie gem that provides some much needed love, positivity, and chill vibes. If you're also someone who resides within the Venn Diagram of "Puzzle Game Lover," "Visual Novel Enthusiast," and "Enjoyer of Queer Games," then Spirit Swap is absolutely worth your time and attention.

DeadOS is a great zombie simulator similar to the old Zombie Infection Simulator, but better. Though currently light on content, it has a lot of potential to be a great modern zombie apocalypse simulator. You can customize everything from the size of the city, how many people live there, how many are police or infected, ect. Something I found neat while playing is that you can control people manually, even if they're already infected/zombified, and the accessibility opions allow you to change the indicator colors as well as the ability to turn the retro lines off (It started to hurt my eyes after around an hour). I do have a few suggestions, though:

1. Make the cars a bit stronger, as they get destroyed when you run over one or two people.
2. Have a "wait" option when controlling a person so that you don't have to struggle though large crowds as much or end up getting stuck in them.
3. A steam workshop where you can share and download custom buildings or other content.
4. Make keybinds for moving up/down floors, speeding up time/slowing it down, and pausing.

Overall, I highly recommend this simulator to everyone that loves watching retro people scream, suffer and get killed either from a zombie or from military brutality.

An incredibly enjoyable shooter made in Doom Engine or whatever it's called. Cohesive story, satisfying gunplay, subtle comedy, interesting levels, solid art direction, honestly just incredible all around. Lots of content, on top of lots of replayability. I would recommend this to anyone who's looking for an FPS, whether you're a fan of hardcore difficulty or just like a story with some action; the difficulty settings make the game very accessible, but isn't for first time gamers.

The rest of this review is just specifics about my experience.

Personally, I consider myself pretty good at games, but this can get SUPER difficult. I had to play a bit to find out what I was comfortable with. I was trying to gauge how much ammo I had as a metric for how well I was doing, but even when I had no issues with ammo, I would get obliterated if I wasn't ready. It offers a challenging experience with lots of room for player growth.

I really enjoy the environments and storytelling. I can tell that every corner of every level is thoughtfully considered. An incredible amount of work went into everything, especially the levels, and it shows. The atmosphere is great, and very consistent. Being able to unravel the story piece by piece is really nice too, especially since a lot of it isn't in your face. There's plenty PLENTY of environmental storytelling, it's very well done. Most of everything else is done through "datapads," or your typical "find notes in the world" method of storytelling, so there's reading, but it's never a lot at once. They're short and spaced out so that my ADHD brain can hang on just long enough to read them.

The story itself is interesting. It's not complicated (from what I can tell), but it's enough that there's mystery and enough worth figuring out as you play through the game. Of course, the story isn't done as of this review, so I'm just talking about the first chapter. It's never too much, but it's written in a way that takes itself seriously. It feels just right for a shooter game that respects both players who like a story, and those who just wanna shooty-bang-bang.

Now, this might be too specific, but I wanted to mention it. I think my absolute favorite part about the game was actually the indirect (and direct) storytelling we get about the protagonist, Dawn. You start out with just the little leftover messages and health history, but then you can start to piece some other things together just with what you're doing as her. I'll put specific details in spoilers, just in case you want to find this stuff out for yourself.

[spoiler]Just before the start of the first chapter, Dawn is recently promoted to head of security. She has depression and anxiety, and is being tested for some genetics-related muscular disorder. She has a stuffed bear named Wilson. She has a high score in the arcade game that's mysteriously everywhere. She willingly plays the arcade game (if you choose to) during an emergency. She installs a clicker game on her datapad (if you find it) and plays it, again, during an emergency. And, my favorite, she eats an INCREDIBLE amount of food. If you realize that you can eat food to gain a little health, you can just INHALE food that's laying around. She burps if you eat too much. It was so funny when I found out.[/spoiler]

So, basically what I'm getting at is, despite there never being a lot of text who tells you that Dawn is this way or that way, you can learn a lot about her, and much of it is just, really funny and unexpected. I think they did a fantastic job of characterizing the protagonist in subtle ways. I appreciate that.

Lastly, I should mention... Secrets. There are a LOT of secrets to find. I was unprepared for how much my brain would shout at me to find all of them. You do not need to find ANY of them, but I'm one of those people who tries to 100% things when I like them. So, I spent way too much time fumbling around in silence, looking for hidden things. My playtime could've been paced way better if I had just been normal about the secrets. That's on me. They were very well hidden, and having a little secret-finder is a brilliant idea. But you know, if the environments were boring, I likely would've burnt out, so I thank the devs for that.

If you've read this far, and you think you might experience similar, then my only advice is, DO NOT WORRY TOO MUCH ABOUT THE SECRETS (on your first playthrough). You will have a much better experience if you relax a bit.

Okay, review over. Really great game. Hard to believe there's even more work being done to improve it when it's this good. Thanks, devs.

I love this game, here's some points on why:

-The most important thing in any FPS imho is that it feels good and satisfying to shoot enemies. Selaco nails this better than any other FPS I've played in recent memory, both new and old. The guns feel appropriately powerful and impactful, and enemies die in glorious splatters of blood and giblets with sound effects that really sell it. It all comes together to make the game just feel really good to play.

-Level design is gorgeous and the spaces you fight through are believable without sacrificing navigation and pacing. There's so much to interact with in fun little ways that have no reason to be there other than to give the game more details and it really helps the game's world feel that much more like an actual place rather than merely the setting in which you fight.

-Sound design is top notch. As stated before, the sound effects do a great job really selling the action. Dialogue is minimal but the enemy radio chatter really shines through. Hearing the enemies start to panic as you tear through their squad helps fuel a sense of power in the player, and the enemy chatter you can hear outside of battle often properly dispels any notion of remorse you may feel for them. The music is absolutely bangin' and fits the mood perfectly in any given circumstance.

-The plot is there to be taken in, but since a lot of it exists via data pads you collect, you can largely ignore it if you're the type who doesn't care. I can't speak too firmly on this point as the story isn't finished yet(and I haven't finished what's already out), but personally I'm intrigued enough so far to engage with the logs I find and read through them.

There's more to be said, but for now I'll simply say I recommend this game to just about anyone who enjoys a good FPS.

A lot of boomer shooters tend to feel kinda samey, like cheap imitations of the real deal. Selaco seems to understand what made the classics tick, and that attention to detail makes Selaco stand out from the crowd. It felt like I was dying of dementia as everything was familiar, yet managed to feel new. 

[h1] The Good: [/h1]
[list]
    [*]The gunplay is very solid. If you've played a lot of the classics in the FPS genre, the weapons will feel suspiciously familiar; the dev's got good taste. 
    [*]Great visual design, sound design, and soundtrack
    [*]Melee is fun. Trying to play through this game with only your fists makes you feel like you are dying of dementia
    [*]Lots of amusing secrets and easter eggs
    [*]AI that stays interesting. There's a mildly concerning amount of interactions with them
    [*]Surprisingly high skill ceiling with neat techs
    [*]The oldschool-style lack of guidance in the level design made me feel like I was dying of dementia
    [*]Dev team is pragmatic and open to feedback
[/list]

[h1] Caveats: [/h1]
[list]
    [*]Gameplay can change significantly between updates, though you have full access to previous versions
    [*]Their choice of engine might come back to haunt them
    [*]Some weapons may be harder to use than others
    [*]Most upgrades are obtained by exploring the map and/or looking for secrets
    [*]The oldschool-style lack of guidance in the level design made me feel like I was dying of dementia
[/list]

[h1] The Bad [/h1]
Note: I probably won't be keeping this list up to date
[list]
    [*]The majority of the time, I did not end up using all the tools at my disposal:

    A lot of weapon upgrades were either not very useful or were just minor QoL.

    Ice grenades feel redundant. 

    A lot of the weapon attachments were overshadowed by the ones that are objectively stronger. 

    The reverse weapon bloom of the nail gun can make it unwieldy at times. I'd prefer it if it was a fixed, but wide-ish spread. 

    You are more likely to survive by staying at 35 HP, rather than using your medkits.

    [*]Readability can be very rough around the edges, but it has been improving. Also, smoke particles only blind yourself for the most part. 
    [*]You're sometimes unable to quicksave because a manhack got stuck somewhere, but won't de-aggro

    [*]The fact that enemies are 2D sprites can make them sneakier than intended, and flying enemies end up being awkward to fight as a result. 
    [*]The.. [i]detail[/i] with the mirrors. 
    [*]The oldschool-style lack of guidance in the level design made me feel like I was dying of dementia
[/list]

Jokes aside, the way forward was easy to miss either because my eyes drifted elsewhere, or I got distracted looking for secrets. [h3]AMAZING[/h3]
Highly recommend this for pretty much anyone.

Transforming wastelands into verdant paradises is a charming experience. The game is unique, fun and challenging while also being approachable and relaxing. 

The gameplay never feels repetitive, and there's exactly the right amount of content -- each area presents its own unique mechanics and challenges relating to the logistics of power and water, so I never had the sense of "oh, it's just *this* again." It's very thoughtfully designed.

It's so rewarding to play that even when I've messed up and had to completely restart a stage, I've actually looked forward to working back from the beginning with my newly acquired knowledge -- but don't worry, restarting stages isn't likely something you'll have to do very often as long as you're paying attention. The difficulty balance is just enough to keep you focused.

[h3]BUT...[/h3]
IMO there's a significant issue with the stage ordering. The world map gives you a % meter for how much of the planet you've reclaimed which is your main sense of progress between stages, and you expect to finish the game when you get it to 100%. However, the "final" mission is actually available when you've only done around half of the planet, and you aren't even aware it's the final mission until you're most of the way through it--so if you've just chosen it randomly, bad luck to you. It would actually be a very sweet and satisfying ending if it didn't come early and out of nowhere. It makes it feel as though the rest of the planet doesn't need saving so you may as well pack up and go home -- kinda undermines the satisfaction.

Fortunately you CAN continue playing to reclaim the rest of the planet in what I guess is a sort of "post-game" and I've read that there's another (much less satisfying) ending once you do that. Just would've been nice not to have been blindsided by credits.

[h1]RUNNING IN THE 90'S[/h1]
Do you ever get that one game where you ask yourself why is this game not getting more attention? To me, that’s [b]Victory Heat Rally (VHR)[/b]. I first heard of this game while going through [b]Twitter[/b] and was intrigued by its art style. I then found out it was on [b]Steam[/b], saw some of its gameplay and I was immediately hooked by it. Like I fell in love with playing the game, so much that I got all the achievements

[h1]Pros and Cons[/h1]
[b]Pros[/b]
[list]
[*]Very fun gameplay that is easy to pick up and play
[*]12 different characters for you to play as, each with their own unique stats
[*]Really nice upbeat soundtrack
[*]Beautiful retro arcade racing-style graphics
[/list]

[b]Cons[/b]
[list]
[*]The gameplay can get repetitive after a while
[/list]

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
[b]VHR[/b] is an arcade-styled racing game where you race against 11 other racers, which is very easy to pick up and play. This is very nice for those who just want an easy arcade-style racing game for you to go and play. For those looking for an arcade game with some minor challenge, then this game has that too. I feel that this is a game that can appeal to almost anyone who is looking for a casual fun racing game. Unless you are looking for a racing game with some challenge, then [b]VHR[/b] won’t really be the racing game for you, as the game as a whole isn’t really that hard.

You can race on various tracks; some will be long and have three laps, and some will be smaller but have four or five laps, then there is rally racing, although it’s not a proper rally race. You will sometimes lap other racers, but you can crash into their cars to knock them off the track for a bit, the game encourages you to do this as there are three achievements to it. There are three main game modes for you to play, these are [b]Arcade GP, Championship mode[/b], and [b]time trails[/b] mode.

When your car is drifting you can build up this meter, when you let go you will be giving a burst of speed. The boost meter has three levels to it, so the longer you hold it down, the more boost you get to help you get ahead of other racers. The boost meter speed is dependent on the weight of the car you are driving, while the speed of your boost is dependent on your power. Although weight is also dependent on how far you push other racers. Speed will affect your top speed when boosting is not in effect, acceleration is how fast you get to your top speed and handling affects how sharp you can make your turns.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3420474844
There are 12 different racers for you to choose from and each has their stats that are unique to them. However, you can tweak them by having different gear or tires for them that can raise or lower a certain state depending on which one you have on you. My favorite character to play is Tommy because I could make his speed, and acceleration good, with some nice handling. Although all racers are viable in their ways with the right stats, you just have to go out of your way to experiment on them.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3420474219
You start with three racers but to unlock more you will have to beat them in a race to unlock them in [b]championship mode[/b]. In this mode, you and the rival racer will have a health bar and if you are a certain distance from them, it will deplete. If you or the rival racer are a certain distance away from each other, the health bar will deplete faster.

The game does have some to do with it. There are also some minigames that you can play in [b]championship mode[/b]. However, other than that, the gameplay can get rather repetitive. Even when I got all the achievements, there was nothing really left to do in the game.

[h1]Graphics and Performance[/h1]
[b]VHR's[/b] art style has an arcade-like feel that I liked very much. The areas all felt different, but they were all colorful. I tested the game on an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 3GB, AMD Ryzen 5 1500X Quad-Core Processor 3.50, and 16 GB of RAM. I experienced no issues while playing, and the game should be able to run on almost any computer.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3420476264
[h1]Final Verdict[/h1]
I have to honestly say that [b]VHR[/b] is a very nice racing game that I had a ton of fun with. I highly recommend this game for those who either want to play an arcade-like racing game or for those who just want a casual game to play. There is also local multiplayer so you can play with a friend and remote play is also available as well. That being said though, I would maybe get this game on a sale if you are a bit skeptical.

You might be wondering, why the negative review after almost 40 hours playtime? It comes down to a catastrophic lack of polish in several key systems. It's clear the game was released in an unfinished state, and just left there.

Terraforming is HORRIBLY implemented. You have three upgrades to the spade, and the improvements are 1 underwhelming, and 2 irreversible. So once you get a bigger spade you cant dig a small hole anymore. And the chisel you get pretty far into the story is pretty much useless for anything other than wholesale destruction. There really isn't a way to sculpt the land in any sort of detail without excruciating frustration.

The water mechanics are just... bad. That wouldn't be a problem, but irrigation is a massive part of growing your garden.

There are almost no base building options. You sleep in a lean-to on the ground, and store your stuff in four varieties of baskets. There's two types of square path that doesn't really fit into any build other than a square one, and some meh looking walls. There are some nifty lamps tho. It's clear the construction system was an afterthought.

Now, the reasons I stuck with the game for so long before giving up in sheer frustration- the concept is great, the exploration is fun, so is the flying once you get the cloak of winds, and the gardens you cultivate really can look incredible. If only managing them wasn't such an absolute pain in the rear. But most of all, the devs managed to create a great ambience between the graphics, the scale of the world, the music and the lore.

All in all, this game needed a lot more development, either before or after launch. But it seems like there's no chance of further updates. Which is a damned shame, as the bones of a cult classic are there. All that was needed was more polish, fleshing out of the mechanics, some quality of life improvements to the terraforming. I could even deal with the annoying water mechanics, if I just had a way to play around with the terrain without wanting to alt-tab every couple minutes. I can only speculate why this was left the way it is. Underwhelming sales figures? Maybe the itch this game scratches is simply too niche.

A damned shame, if you ask me.

This is a uniquely beautiful foraging game. Once you get the hang of the world and growing plants, I found this game to be both cozy enough for a weeknight but engaging enough for a full Saturday. I'd recommend this game to anyone who enjoys forage-y, cozy, sandbox-y games - there's no time limits or anything and you can build your own garden. "Garden" is an understatement; more of a stunning oasis with a very simple planting strategy (i.e. not like a complex farming sim). the story itself is well done too, but honestly I was just obsessed with all of the plants, seeds, landscapes, etc.

This game has a great mix of unique post-apocalyptic vibes, with plenty of improvements that make life easier but harder things accessible.

There are improvements to tools, to bases, to watering, to eating, to fighting, to locomotion, to recipes, to making resources last longer.

And you really feel like you are helping take back and restore the land from those who caused the disaster in the first place.

There are so many little game mechanics all mixed together that under normal circumstances, they would be jarring, but the game authors have managed to make them work together.

You start out with so little and try to hunker down close to water and out of the blazing sun, making more forays at night and hoping you make it back before the sun rises too high.

I won't spoil how the world opens up for you over time, and how much the game makes it feel like you earned every last bit of it.

I got a bit too tired by the end to do all the plant challenges, and there's something wrong with the spirit darter invitations where they don't seem to get the message, and I really wish there was a way to cleanse more of the world, but this was a really satisfying game experience.
