Reading numerous positive reviews and buzz surrounding this game prior to my purchase, I did have reservations. I’ve never played an RPG like this, mainly the only type of RPGs I’ve played have all been 3D, AAA games since the PlayStation One. 
If you don’t love JRPGs/RPGs this game isn’t for you. BUT, Octopath Traveller 2 is the type of game you have to play at least once in your life. Simply, if we were to avoid any negative connotations that one might have to RPGs, it is an adventure game. I hear the term that it’s an “old-school RPG”, and while that might true, this game would an amazing RPG regardless of the era it would be released in. This game is easily worth full price.

Personally I had fun with the story, and I can’t stop listening to the soundtrack even after I finished the game (I hadn’t been this moved by a soundtrack/OST since the movie/anime Your Name/Kimi No Na Wa). The music is diverse and fitting for the areas of the game yet they all individually standout. The only downside to the music is that this game didn’t have AAA marketing behind it so it’s a true shame we may never see orchestras play OT2’s music live.

 
There is a pleasant flow and rhythm to the menuing and the battles, making it enjoyable to manage your resources while simultaneously maximising your opportunities in battle. Battles are easy if you plan your moves, but the tide can turn if you lose focus. I never found the battle system tiresome (maybe due to the amazing music) that I was able to grind my way to level 90+ mostly. Beyond the battle system, the way the characters and the story interact with the world and NPCs is entertaining too. I spent 100+ hours on this game, and every action, decision, felt meaningful.


For a long time, I’ve been wanting Square to remake one of my favourite Final Fantasy’s. But since playing this game, I question is that really necessary? Even if a beloved game is remade with modern graphics and soundtrack…. Would it give me the same feeling of excitement and wonder that is experienced when you play an amazing game for the first time? Octopath Traveller 2 is a game that does just that. That feeling of playing an amazing RPG for the first time.. and giving you feelings you’ve never experienced before. That is something remakes can’t do.  I’m playing FF7 Rebirth right now, and as a fan of FF7 Remake and the OG FF7… I think because of OT2 I’m not enjoying as much as I would hope. I don’t want to compare the games, but when I explore the rich, beautiful crafted world—that you question the necessity of the requirement for high graphical fidelity… Somehow, despite the lack thereof Octopath Traveller 2 really immerses you in the environment… and captivates you with the charm of its characters and mesmerise you with its music… OT2, perhaps momentarily, stops you from wishing the game you want to exist… by being the game that you need. 

Thank you for this amazing game, Team Asano.


P.S Despite this game having moments where it is affected by Square’s censorship policies. Despite how much I oppose that, it still doesn’t diminish how much I love this game. That’s how much I love Octopath Traveller 2.

It took a good long time, but I finally beat it. Octopath traveler 2 is probably the finest JRPG I have ever played. If you are looking for a good, long game to really sink your teeth into, this is it.

By far and away the best thing about this game is the music. It is the best soundtrack of any video game I have ever played. Truth be told, I actually bought this game when it first came out, but life got busy and eventually I stopped playing. What finally brought me back was thinking about how good that music was. What makes it better is that almost every piece in the game has two versions, a fully orchestrated day version and a thinly orchestrated night version. I tend to prefer the night versions, I appreciate the simplicity of the piano scores, but the day versions are also very good.

Aside from that, the world of this game is very good and full of surprises. You really want to explore every corner of this game because there are so many different things to find. You can even buy a ship at one point and sail around like you could in the old Final Fantasy games. The boss fights are super good, they are each interesting and have their own twist, but don't take forever to beat like they did in the original Octopath Traveler. Speaking of which, this game improves on a lot about that game. It has a much larger, more complete world and a lot of the mechanics that were bad or difficult in that game are back in a much better form. I appreciate that you can skip the chapter one of each character and come back and do it later, makes the game much more replayable.

My biggest gripe with the game is the encounter rate. There are way too many enemies. Make sure you get the evasive maneuvers passive skill early on, or else have some way to kill enemies quickly, otherwise you will go insane. The game does feel a bit grindy at times, but it is not too bad, you can often avoid grinding by taking a good path through the story.

The story itself is very good. Like the first game, there are eight separate stories all tied together with one overarching story. The separate stories are good for the most part, but they tend to be a bit basic. The overarching story really brings it together in a neat way, it is worth playing all the way through just for that. The characters are also pretty good, Throne's my favorite (and from what I've seen I think she is everyone's favorite). I also really liked Partitio, Osvald, and Hikari. I have mixed feelings about Temenos, Agnea, and Ochette. Castti was the only one I didn't like, she tended to come off as annoying, even if her story was actually pretty good (except for chapter 2: Sai route, probably my least favorite chapter in the game).

With all that said, yes, I do absolutely recommend this game. If you are a fan of JRPGs, you will love it. Even if you aren't I think it is worth giving it a try. I am mixed on JRPGs as a genre if I am telling the truth, but this game is one that I do very much enjoy.

Review: This is a beautiful game with exciting story telling, and smart combat. It is also great to have various play throughs interacting with different characters at different point in their stories. Being able to mix up strategies and what party you will lead as your main, creating an almost different form of gameplay is enjoyable. i didn't find myself bored of any of the protagonist or their motivations.  

This is a gorgeous representation of classic RPG being brought into modern games and audience. If you ever wanted to share the joy that these types of games brought you with someone who hasn't experienced that childhood glee, or even someone who is missing it now as an adult, this is the game. The only thing that prevents this from being a 10/10 is the lack of customization. One of the things I really enjoy in modern RPG's is the ability to really immerse myself into a character or group of characters. Being able to dress them up in style's I feel benefit the story I'm playing is fun. Finding loot that directly impacts the way my character comes across is nice. It really adds to the world building for me. Not to say that there isn't any customization which these characters. (When you sub class them they take on the outfits of the additional class) It just wasn't what I pictured from this sequel.   

TLDR: Gorgeous game. Grind heavy game. Fun and varied game. Top rated RPG in my catalog (Top 5 for me personally).  Would Recommend.

[b]Cons:[/b]
* The audio balance is a bit off in this game. One character talks so quietly that they're often overpowered by the music and another one peaks the mic. I want to stress that the voice acting is really good. There is nothing wrong with the performances themselves. I have to wonder if there was something wrong with the hardware or something? I suggest that the author plays a couple of this type of games first to get a general idea of the concept. 
Have a look at e.g. Zombie Exodus. In this "interactive novel" here I got to choose whether I wear blue trousers or skinny jeans and that is pretty much all I can do during hundreds of screens. 

Next, next, next, next, next... Clicking on the NEXT button seems to be the only interaction here. Wow, I unlocked several achievments by clicking NEXT a couple of times. Hey what about if you let me decide how I want the story to go? This is garbage.

Most characters were well made with credible personality and i'd say half the choice were relevant/suitable all the while the pacing isn't bad.

 -the way the story push you in the direction of Callum is a big turn off : Seriously, in the stats he was despising me and almost killed me(and there's too many time where he made the situation dire by his stupidity/ dangerous behavior) but the game tried to force a romance out of it..

 -Many thing are wrong and/or stupid within the story and how it unfold (i obviously don' ask for a "realist" zombie game, but at last don't make the character a bunch of moron to help the scenario)

If you want to go back to high school and remember the thrill of having adventures with your friends, while building friendships and trying to survive band camp... then this game is for you! (Attention to the word "survival" because the game becomes dark, friends. Be careful!) The dialogues are fun and the protagonist is certainly one of the best characters in the game! WHAT A BADASS!  So let's get to the routes...

And the first route played was Peter's. Peter is a controversial guy that you want to kiss and punch at the same time, he may be a little shit but there's no denying he's charming. Even though I didn't like the way he and the protagonist got together (you have to respect girl code, as Susie said) and [spoiler]how he broke up with Felicity (I mean, that was a big no no)[/spoiler], he managed to redeem himself in the final chapters. <3 In the end, the route was very sweet and we found out that he is a romantic and protective guy. I like characters that evolve over the course of the story and I think Peter has great character development. In short, he managed to make me completely fall in love.

Garth's route was the second one I did and … wow, I definitely DIDN'T EXPECT this one![spoiler]I was curious to know how he had just disappeared in Peter's route and here we find out what happened[/spoiler] Poor Garth! In fact, I particularly recommend leaving this route for the finale, as it can give you anxiety about playing the final route. [spoiler]It's also pretty short as it ends in Chapter 6 (for reasons I can't reveal).[/spoiler]

The next one was… Tom. If in Peter's route the romance already starts in the first chapters, in this route things only unfold towards the end. Tom's route is like a "common route" with several characters appearing and helping you. It really represents "friendship"! As for the romance... well, those who like friends to lovers will like it, it's a cute route and has several flashbacks to how they met and became friends. I haven't played all the routes yet, but it's almost like this is the "true route" (as much as I don't like that term). It was a cute and heart warming route!

And next is Clark! Oh god, that route went from heaven to hell real quick. I mean, in the beginning it was incredibly funny and the dynamic between Clark and Cadence was amazing! Bullying Clark has become one of my favorite activities (sorry not sorry Clark). But then... BOOM! Everything started to fall apart. And once again the protagonist shows why she is the most BADASS character in this game! (Did I ever say she's the best character? No? SHE IS! Forget the boys, Cadence is the best!). And Clark, well, I'd say one minute you want to protect him from the world's hate and the next you want to drown him in a lake while the leeches take care of him.. Don't expect too much romance in this route either, actually there's less than Tom's (but at least he has the best epilogue so far). And Tom... oh Tom, I'm starting to see why they say you're the best boy <3 I'll never forget your loyalty. I really don't know what to say about this route, there were so many different emotions, but it has several of my favorite moments.

And then comes Poptart… … … I heard there is a Poptart Protection Association? Is that true? Where do I sign up to become a member? My heart ached here, I won't deny it. It's a pretty heavy route. [spoiler]I have a bit of a problem with yanderes, but I think his troubled past justified it well.[/spoiler] The ending was pretty emotional too, the whole second home story got me. [spoiler]And Bandit helping find Melvin at the end was perfect. <3[/spoiler] THESE ROUTES ARE BREAKING ME DOWN AND STILL 3 LEFT! (Will I be able to survive Band Camp?)

And next is Samuel. And I thought that Peter's route was the charming and romantic one in the game, but Sam is not far behind! Samuel is chill and his and Cadence's dynamic is super cute! If on Clark's route everything that can go wrong does go wrong, I'd say that on this one everything goes smoothly (Or is it just because it's my sixth route? I don't know). Sam is a calm person and his route is just like him, sweet and calm [spoiler](I mean, if even Mr. Wiley's heart was touched, then how can we poor mortals resist?) <3[/spoiler]

And the last one (before the big finale) is Doug! Sorry to leave you last, Doug, but you're not my type lol. Overall, it was a pretty fun route, mostly because of the drummers dynamic. Also, we can also get to know Marian better, I didn't think I would like her so much! And it's one of the routes with the best epilogue! (super sweet) The fact that Alex falls in love with a different girl on each route kills me lol XD This kid has the potential to be even worse than Petter!

And then the final route… BEST ROUTE! It's it. As much as I love romance, the best thing about this game isn't the romance, it's seeing the marching band family dynamic and we get a lot of that on this route. A reward for suffering. <3 Garth is also very cute in this route, love him <3 [spoiler]And Mr. Savage's case finally revealed, I didn't expect that from Felicity <3[/spoiler] And obviously… AARONNN <3 I loved the moments with him (Fandisk with his route when? XD)

It's hard to pick a favorite guy, everyone managed to charm me in some way, but in the end... my favorite was Peter <3 and then Tom and Clark <3

Thus far, I have only completed two endings, both of them bad. However, despite witnessing horrors beyond comprehension and crying once more over a fictional man, I can say this:

This game is phenomenal.

No, no, hear me out. When you Google Band Camp Boyfriend, the label "survival game" pops up under it. For those of you unfamiliar with marching band, every rehearsal is a matter of survival. High school, college, or drum corps, you need to be there and be dedicated if you expect to survive. BCB is no different. It keeps you on your toes. You wanted a silly little otome game, you are both in the right place and the wrong one. Think Fujiwara Bittersweet: cute and silly on the outside, but it could jump out at you when you least expect it.

But a marching band otome, you say, doesn't that [i]sound[/i] silly? Oh, it absolutely is. Expect some fourth wall breaking while you're at it. If you're a marching band kid like I am, you're going to laugh, and you're going to cry. Every single character is probably going to remind you of someone in your own marching band, from Poptart the mellophone rookie to Tom the bonehead. Even Mr. Wiley, bless his beard, might give you horrible flashbacks, depending on the scene. ("WHO WROTE THIS DRILL?" "You did, sir.") All of these characters and scenes are a labor of love and marching band nostalgia, and having just finished up my final marching season myself this year, it is a welcome turn down memory lane.

Even if you’re not familiar with marching band, there’s a helpful glossary that pops up every time a marching band phrase is used. Your band might not be quite like the Marching Bandits, you’ll find yourself wanting to hang out with these kooky kids. They’ll become your family soon enough, even if you do want to punch them occasionally (Felicity, I’m looking at you). There is something charming about each of the possible boyfriends, and while Tom is most certainly my favorite (I like a guy who can make me laugh), Peter has to be a close second. Sometimes. Even then, I find myself loving every single character and wanting to experience four years of marching band with them.

That said, it’s not all sunshine and rainbows. Yes, on the outside, this is a fancy free band camp story, but there is a reason the devs put [url=https://lovebirdgames.com/warnings/]content warnings[/url] in the game and on their website. Some bonkers stuff happens. As you’re reminded often—almost creepily so—this is a video game. It could get weird at any second. And oh, does it. That said, please take care of yourself, and if you don’t want to get messed up like I did (whoops), follow the helpful walkthroughs on Lovebird Games’s website to help you get only the happy stuff.

Yet even though I despise bad endings and try my best not to get them in most of the games I play… the ones I did play are very well done. Is any of this believable? Well, I certainly hope not. Do the endings HIT? Oh, absolutely. There is no beating around the bush. You’re not getting out of this season easily. But along the way, at least you get some nice, sweet moments and cute smiles from the marching band boy of your dreams. (Tom is everything to me now. EVERYTHING.) Be careful out there, kids.

As for the romance itself, though I’ve only been experiencing the wonder and hilarity of Tom (no wonder he’s last in the recommended order, he’s too funny), what I’ve gotten so far has been exceptional. Yes, I’m still blushing from some of the things he’s said or done. Yes, I’m entirely sure Peter would do that to me, too (he was already halfway there when I was maybe-sorta flirting with him as well as Tom). I’m confident that the rest of the routes do something along these same lines. Like I said, every boy in this game is lovable in some way (even Drum and Drummer), and the romance is just soft and sweet enough that anything else that comes your way will hopefully pale in comparison.

I could go on about how much I love the witty banter in the writing, or the fact that the pause button is the musical notation for a grand pause, or the amazingly detailed and careful art by an artist I’ve seen before and absolutely ADORE… but I won’t. You’ll have to experience that for yourself. I am absolutely biased toward this game that I’ve been waiting for since I was a freshman in my college marching band. My marching band blood makes me automatically love this game because of its subject matter. But it is not a lie to say this is a wonderful first game made by very caring and considerate developers who poured their entire beings into this. As a member of their Discord server, I have happily eaten up the WIP Wednesdays and slowly fallen in love with the characters through Screenshot Saturdays. In a world full of devs who turn out to be selfish or greedy or just plain rude, these devs are awesome. I love them and their work dearly, and I’m so happy that I stumbled upon this game entirely by accident back when it was still just a demo.

Now why the hell did you read this entire review? GO PLAY THE GAME!!!

Band Camp Boyfriend is a charming indie game with a music theme that impresses with its excellent art and sound design. It takes place in a band camp and offers players the chance to shape the story through branching story-lines and multiple endings, providing an enjoyable and immersive experience. As an Otome game, Band Camp Boyfriend features a compelling and immersive narrative that will appeal to both fans of the genre and newcomers. 

The game's humor and jokes are well-executed and kept me entertained throughout. Overall, Band Camp Boyfriend is a must-play for anyone looking for an engaging and fun gaming experience. Some of the music terminology went over my head, but I do not feel it is necessary to enjoy the game.

BCB is about you, the drum major as you try to survive band camp and its unpredictable events, characters and ofc a love interest of your own. [h1] Gameplay [/h1]

The overlook and use of the game is clear cut and easy to access, there are a lot of save slots and even autosave. Some buttons are confusing like how yes and music note can both be clicked on, the return button on alma mater is a little hard to click on too. But it is not  a showstopper,and nothing has crashed for me so its all good.

[h1] Characters [/h1]

This is an order from best to worst, just my personal opinion so dont come after me ,,

[list]
    [*]Aaron
Does he have a route? No. Am I going to include him anyway? Yes. Aaron is my FAVOURITE i love him so much he got me squealing and stuff. He bullies everyone and I love him. If he kicked me id thank him. If you wanna make another route, im begging you take Aaron. Okay moving onto actual routes now.

Also another definite 3 dimensional character, him being smart underneath it all but still being his lighthearted carefree self. His character is written spectacularly, doesnt raise any eyebrows. His route felt personal, final and since hes friends with anything and anyone you get to interact with so many different characters here. He is so lovable. [spoiler] Tom’s bad ending is the only one that made me cry. Heartbreaking, I love it sm [/spoiler]

This is one of the best games I have ever had the pleasure to play. This game was everything I could have wanted out of a band game and more! As a dating sim, it is incredibly diverse and fun with seven different guys that you can all befriend and romance. Not only are the LI's diverse in character, they're diverse in their perspectives on band and what band means to them. Some touched me more than others, however all of the boys and their stories are winners. If you are here for a fun dating sim, this is a great game to play! If you want to experience marching band again, then this game couldn't be more perfect for you.

Below, I'm going to write down a summary on what each of the boys are like and how I felt about all of their routes. [spoiler]The final route[/spoiler] will be brought up as well as I feel that is the most rewarding story told in the entirety of the game. I played this in the recommended route order on the Lovebird Games website, so let's go ahead and get started!

1. Peter: Oh Peter! I can understand how he was the first LI to date. His route has a little bit of everything. Good comedy, great chemistry with your character, other characters having growth of their own, some hilarious high school drama, some painful angst, all of it! His route is very fun to play. I actually was not bothered by how [spoiler] him and Cadence get together. Of course it's a crappy thing to get with a  girl while you're still with your soon to be ex-girlfriend, but how you two get together fits him as a character super well. [/spoiler] His route is very strong overall and I'm really glad he was my first taste of this crazy game! 

2. Doug: Oh sweet sweet Doug. The biggest bass drum player and dummy in the band! For what he lacks in brains he more than makes up for his big heart. Doug is very impulsive and [spoiler] gets you two into hot shit by yeeting the pit instruments into the lake [/spoiler] yet I wasn't as bothered by that as other players were. I wasn't a huge fan of his chemistry with the MC but his route overall is still amazing! A testament to how well written this game is!

3. Clark: The one that made this game good to literal masterclass for me. I will not lie, this review may be a little all over the place as this was my favorite LI and [spoiler] romantic route [spoiler] from the entire game. He is a grumpy, wet cat. An angry little ball of fluff. He has doubted you from the very start and is pissed you took the drum major position from him. I did not like him at first until [spoiler] the apology and the end of Peter's route where you rescue him from the fire [/spoiler]. I saw that and thought: "Wow, this kid is insane! I want to study him under a microscope". When I saw he was up next after Doug, I was very surprised but excited. Poptart, Peter, and him were the three characters that really grabbed my attention during the beginning of the game. I wish I could describe how hyped I felt booting up the game when I started his route. After playing it, I can say with upmost certainty that his is my favorite route. Everything about it was damn perfect to me. [spoiler] The coffee date where you see him loosen up a bit and his theme plays for the first time, which is also where you learn how deeply he loves music and band. The conducting lesson, both of the scenes where you walk in each other in PJs. Him showing you Radon Cat and talking about Cole. All the hell he and you go through in the second half of his route, where you almost lose all of your friends and put everyone in danger by arguing that staying in camp with a deranged Mr. Wiley is safer than leaving. Him purposely ignoring you and trying to break off your friendship because he doesn't want you to be ostracized like he is. The implication being that he loves you too much to ever have you go through the pain he has dealt with for years. The argument you two have on the band field and him finally admitting that he was wrong and the absolute implication that he felt like staying would be safer for everyone was because he was terrified of Mr. Wiley, of what he could do. Him telling Mr. Wiley that Cadence is the best drum major the band has ever had, especially if you had played other routes before his, is so amazing, his breakdown in the woods, and both of you apologizing to the band for everything are so wonderful. THE KISS AFTER THE PERFORMANCE!!! Literally the best slowburn romance in the whole game for me!!! This route is no joke. Both Cadence and Clark go through hell in it and the band is easily at it's worst in this route. Yet, the payoff is so worth it in the end! The band is at it's best it ever is besides the final route. Clark has genuinely become an amazing leader due to knowing Cadence and he shows that. Their final CG where they are a drum major power couple together is the best thing ever, I love it so much!! His love of band and music resonated with me so hard, that it made me cry and want to play my trombone again. He also has some similar characteristics to me as well. I won't lie, he is quite literally me from highschool minus the being a jerk aspect of his character. I love him so much. [/spoiler] There is so much more I could write about with these two but then I would literally forget the other characters! This is a route that should be saved for later, as I feel it gets more rewarding the later you play it in game.

4. Samuel: The coolest of cool! After the emotional intensity of Clark's route, Samuel's route is a refreshing change of pace. He is very quiet but not because he dislikes people. He just is in his own little world a lot and like him, it is a nice reprieve from the wildness of band. He has the most romantic route besides Peter. Despite how chill his route is, there is still a lot of depth to him that we learn as we go further into the route. I want to give specific praise for [spoiler] how Samuel has to deal with microaggressions nearly every day at band, especially from Mr. Wiley. I also appreciate the he is made to be more than the "one black kid" in band. That the reason he plays is his family and that he comes from a history of jazz saxophone players! I felt that was especially poignant considering that Jazz is a black art form and that his grandfather was likely alive during the bossa nova and bebop era of jazz! You managed to write him with the same amount of respect as Peter and white and I appreciate that so much! [/spoiler]

Garth: He deserved better.

Poptart: My sweet baby gremlin boy! He was my second favorite LI in this game besides Clark! His route will gut you but his wholesome dynamic with Cadence balances things out in my opinion. One thing I have to praise is [spoiler] how you wrote his abuse from his perspective. That you gave him the power to talk about his experience as a survivor. The perspective shift is powerful, along with learning his real name. His philosophy that band is family rings so true. It's part of why I love him as a character so much! [/spoiler]

Tom: His route did so much to characterize Cadence. He also is incredibly sweet and has been friends with you, your character, for years! His route is a nice ending before the final route as [spoiler] everyone in the band gets along and even develop in ways they don't in other routes besides that one. It's a taste of what's to come! [/spoiler] Save this one for last! It is incredibly satisfying to play.

I actually am running out of word space, so I will not be able to say much about the Final route beyond that: You need to play it and [spoiler] it is the best route of the entire game, hands down. It recontextualizes the entire game and changes your whole opinion on a certain band director...[/spoiler]

This is all I can fit right now, but I hope this is a good review for you all who read it : ) Thank you!

This game is amazing.

The writing is strong, the characters are all wonderful; and designed and written in a realistic way. 

The story comes together to tell the tale of a relatively broke marching band trying to learn The Planets by Holst for a competition, and you play as the drum major; student conductor. 

The player character is funny, she's connected to all the other characters in a way that feels warm and real, and the friendships feel genuine.

The sadder parts of the story are approached with sensitivity, and there's a great deal of care put into the tonal balancing throughout all the routes.

The romance is suitably written for high school students, and is all very sweet and with the usual concerns the age group face.

This is a good game, by a small group, clearly made with a bunch of heart.

I am not typically one for dating sims, but this game has a lot of heart. You can tell that from the writing and storytelling, graphics and design, and music atmosphere that this was a labor of love from start to finish. 

As someone who was in the pit in marching band my freshman year, and then transitioned to bass drum, I really wanted to like Doug, but I found myself drawn a lot more to Sam's calmness and Garth's fun loving, yet ambitious spirit. There's a lot of great references that anyone who has attended band camp will understand, recognize, and be able to connect with on a personal level. All of the characters have such human qualities and characteristics. You want to get to know them better and ask the right questions!

The only critiques I have are those that would probably be fixed with a larger budget. I'd like more voiceover of the conversations, but the work that has been done is well executed and is sprinkled in just enough to keep your imagination engaged while pushing the story forward. It may even be purposeful, but I'm newer to the genre.

Make sure you save your progress as you go, and don't be afraid to let your heart guide you! You'll have fun and be glad you did.

This is exactly my kind of silliness. Shotgun King is a chess game except you only have your king left and he has a shotgun. If that makes you think "Wait a minute, that's not chess at all!" then you would be correct. The game only wears its chess influence only on the surface, the game actually is a turn-based strategy roguelike. You have to play through 12 rounds and defeat the final boss at the end. Each round your goal is to kill the white king. You can do this by firing your shotgun, each white piece have different amount of HP, pawns and knights have the lowest and the king has the most. Your shotgun has three main stats: firepower, range and firing arc. Firepower defines how many pellets your shotgun fires, each pellet dealing exactly one damage. Multiple pellets can hit the same target, can hit multiple targets or completely miss any target. There is some RNG involved here but the closer you stand to your target, the more likely you are to hit it. Range shows the maximum travel range of your pellets. Your firing arc shows the spread of your pellets, they will always be inside this arc. Shooting an enemy that stands directly before you will always make all pellets hit him. It's the same concept as in other shooting games, the shotgun is more powerful close range and loses its power the further you stand away. However, sometimes a wider spread might be beneficial to hit more pieces. There are some strategic decisions you can make here.
Shooting or moving will always pass your turn. White pieces will move on their turn and they can move multiple pieces at the same time. They have their own speed stat that defines how many turns they have to wait until they can move.
Moving will also reload your shotgun. This is important, so you can move outside of check and fire on your next turn.
Your shotgun has only limited ammo, which does regenerate but very slowly, so you don't want to kill every piece, you want to focus on the king but still deal with troublesome pieces.

After each floor you will come in contact with the roguelike mechanic of the game, the cards. You get a selection of two different black cards which help you for the rest of the run. These can be simple like more firepower, ammo or range but they also can give you completely new abilites like a melee attack that does not use ammo or grenades, that will hit multiple pieces but can also kill you.
Each black card is tied to a white card. These are upgrades for the white side. They can get more pieces, change how pieces move and give pieces more HP or speed. You will have to evaluate what upgrades you need but also what downsides you can endure in return. One white card that always appears is the white queen after floor 3. You can't escape her, she is everywhere.
Killing a non-pawn piece will give you an edge however. You get their "soul" which you can activate to move in the same pattern as the piece you killed. You can only store one soul but you can get black cards that allow you to store more or have some other synergy with it. These soul cards are best used to get out of check or close the distance to the white king.

The game is incredibly goofy with its concept but its also a challenging strategy game that will take you some time to master. And as you beat th egame, you will start to unlock new difficulty levels that add extra pieces at the start, improve the enemy AI and give the white king more HP. You can also unlock new shotguns that have different starting stats. There is a surprising amount of variety in this small game. The game still gets updates to this day, despite being almost three years old. It's funny, it's challening and it's the exact type of game to play at the evening after a long work day.

TL:DR This is a real hidden gem of a game, absolutely deserves more attention for the excellent design, story and love poured into it. Even if you don't like visual novels you may like this one.

This game...it must have come from a very talented, passionate and I daresay a warm hearted soul. Though its impossible to judge someone's character based solely on a game there is definitely a special type of gratitude that must exist in the mind of someone to pen a story that attempts to flesh out its characters the way this game does.

Typically in doing a review I would focus on the mechanics that make the game but because the story and what I would call the design philosophy of the game is what gives it its heart, the best way to sing its praises is to touch on these things. Its worth mentioning here that kokoro means heart in japanese and that is part of what drew me to this game to see if it could deliver on such potentially cliche or corny premise, I must say it did for me and then some - it surpassed my expectations which is saying a lot. I've played my fair share of games but visual novels usually turn me off.

The story like any good book is engaging to the point of not wanting to put it down, I was fully immersed in what would happen next while also being hooked by the combat and rpg build crafting. It appears simple on the surface but there is a attention to detail that rings throughout including the design of skills and how they interact with each other that give a far deeper experience than might come through on first glance combined with the various choices on build, itemization and combat approach make for one of the best and yet most accessible strategic rpgs I've played.

The are several difficulties to suit your level of challenge or if you are just there for the story ,which is worth it, but I love well designed challenge and this game's battle system will give it to you. I started a second playthrough 70% into the game just to revisit previous choices, I hate replaying most games and can barely be bothered to finish the majority but this was awesome.

I couldn't quite place my finger on it but I realized the combat felt different than normal the dev revealed the game isnt really based on rng, the opponents are programmed to respond to your moves with a great deal of variation in each enemy and combat setup. Apart from the very first section most of the enemies aren't recycled either, they are often treated as one-off unique characters with their own entry and backstory in the bestiary even the unnamed ones and apart from possibly the very first area (and thats still debatable) re-skins arent really a thing. That's a mad level of dedication that only shows the level of care that was put into this game.

Normally, saying this would by hyperbolic but this game isnt just a game - its a piece of art and love letter from the dev.
No story is truly original but this game has unique elements, but mostly just brings together different elements that you *may* have seen elsewhere and executes them very well. 

I could continue to gush about how I came for the combat (loved it) but stayed for the story but, ultimately, its best to encourage you to experience it all for yourself. There are things I could quibble about if I really tried or was in a particularly bad mood  but I'm not! :D I've never done this before but I give this game a 10/10.

Moving on to play the devs first game on steam eagerly waiting a sequel or the dev's next entry. Well done!

This is basically a demo of an open world action RPG built in Unity that provides you with all the gear and tools required to basically stomp your way through the early part of the game with minimal issues so you can get a feel for the gameplay and interface.
However, this game has no story or explanation as to who you are or why you are here, and the beach you start at is filled with gear and items and magic spells you can equip for free so you don't need to work for anything it's all handed to you.
I call it a demo because there is no sense of purpose and since can't save your game (if you can I can't figure out how) then it's just a one off experience that is unfortunately end result a waste of time and pocket change. There are some quest givers to kill skeletons and such, but a main "goal" doesn't seem to exist.
That being said the game itself is quite fun. I enjoyed the battle system, and the ability to dodge roll was a useful mechanic.
I did find the amount of equipment you can use to be a bit excessive. It reminds me of Morrowind a bit, with the amount of things you can layer onto yourself.
The spell system was fine though a bit overpowered. Cool spell effects and sounds and everything works well from the hotbar.
The graphics were quite nice, blur effects were used well for distance, and with my rather low end PC the game ran pretty good with settings such as anti aliasing off.
Unfortunately, this being a large open world action RPG, not having the ability to save or at least an obvious way to do so is a real deal breaker.
At this stage in the game I would not recommend you bother with this until a clearer sense of direction is presented for the future of the title. It's very unfinished and lacks polish and you can't save your progress so it's just a waste of time.

- Randomize the enemy spawn locations across the playing field, when you figure out where they spawn, it's easy to stand over the spot and mash LMB and 3.
- You could potentially add a randomized player attribute upgrade feature in between rounds (or maybe every 5 rounds) like most wave-based rogue-likes out there.

The first 90 minutes or so were decent, but the second half of the game I felt like it wasn't play tested properly, often having sporadic difficulty or puzzles that could use better hints, in addition to many small glitches. In theory it's not a bad game, but it has a lot of small issues that got in a way of me enjoying it, mostly because there are so many cheap ways to die. It feels like you didn't let many people try the game, the issue with the dancing room is very obvious, but maybe because you made the game you don't see it that way.

There were 2 specific dodging mini-games where the difficulty spike felt very abnormal, the hardest one took me like 20 minutes by itself, granted there are only 3 of those rooms that are unreasonably challenging, but I do mean they are like hard for all the wrong reasons, going from a chill puzzle/visual experience to a full trial and error, not to mention VERY touchy hit-boxes. I get a feeling that this game was barely play tested, you could easily face check the hitboxes 100 times during a playthrough, among many small glitches, multiply by a 7 second respawn between each attempt, not the best feeling. Maybe would not be a problem in a different genre, I just feel LOCKS baits you into a relaxing experience, and I certainly feel like it might mislead the audience for a relaxing puzzle game.

I ran into a good number of environmental glitches, you can get stuck in places but usually you can reset a checkpoint (although not always), it's really those few specific areas that can potentially sour the whole thing. The length of this game is a bit difficult to pinpoint because of that difficulty spike, if the developer fixes those sections I would say it's about 2.5 to 3 hours of content, but the repetition with trial and error can add another 1 to 2 hours on top of it, but again it's not content, just an issue with how a few sections are made with very low margin for error. 

For the most part it's a puzzle game with occasional platforming and trap rooms where you can die, I would say 70% puzzles, 20% platforming, 10% 'low to high' difficulty dodging games. Most of the regular puzzles were fine, even enjoyable, but there are definitely maybe like 5 rooms where I wanted to uninstall the game, mainly because you don't always get great visual feedback on what is happening, or what it is exactly you trying to do. The narrative is pretty much 100% visual storytelling, I mean it kinda works, but I don't feel strongly about it one way or another, it was very vague. Maybe it could have used some cozy story moments between 2 characters to set it up better.

[h1] Pros: [/h1]

+ The diorama aesthetic and 'horror vibes' were pretty enjoyable with good variety, lots of different surreal locations, weird environments with some psychological meaning, thing like that, if you in it just for the weird look, at least that part is mostly good.

+ Look dev, I think there are a lot of good puzzles in the game, I mostly enjoyed the sections with the pictures, and it certainly has a lot of mechanical variety which is nice. Granted, the bad puzzles in this game kinda overshadow the good because they take much longer to brute force.

[h1] Feedback: [/h1]

- So the most frustrating part in the game for me was the dance with the spikes, and then the knife game that was also frustrating but not nearly as hard. I am not sure what would be a perfect solution. You could consider giving the player 2 hitpoints instead of 1, making hitboxes smaller, or perhaps allowing the player to skip those 2 if they die 20 times or so.

- I got stuck inside walls or fallen into unintantional floor gaps (I know there is one around the chess board before you make first vertical jump), sometimes you can just press ESC and reload, but sometimes it won't let you press it. I must have opened the game again at least 5 times. Also any way to speed up those respawns cuz 7 seconds for so many ways to die... Mmmmm

- For the regular puzzles, maybe color code the one with 10 numbers, in a way that player can see what he is doing (there are many ways to read that puzzle). On February 5th, I learned about this game’s release and was immediately pleasantly surprised by its visuals and artistic approach. I knew right away that I had to try it!

I instantly went to check out the trailer and screenshots, and what do you think? It really is a puppet theater and a performance within it! The game looks fresh and intriguing. So far, I’ve played for just under three hours, but the puzzles I’ve encountered are interesting and creative. One moment, you’re swapping top and bottom; the next, you're pulling a string to grow bigger, and then something else entirely. Pretty cool! 

Now, as always, let’s break down what I liked, what I didn’t, and some general thoughts.

Pros +: 
+ The Art. It’s gorgeous. The hand-drawn puppet theater style, the constant tension enhanced by parallax effects and horror elements—it’s all fantastic. Sometimes a face peeks at you, sometimes a centipede scurries past, sometimes eerie, corrupted eyes appear. Huge respect to the devs for this!
+ The Puzzles. Engaging, not too difficult (though they do make you think). So far, I’ve only encountered one that I had to brute-force my way through. 😆
+ The Animations. Oh, this is next-level! Every button press makes the strings twitch, as if someone behind the scenes is pulling them. The hand at the beginning moves so naturally—it feels almost alive, yet still retains that theatrical quality. Everything looks delightfully puppet-like. Amazing!
+ It’s scary! Really scary. If only we knew what it was, but... well, you know. 😅 The atmosphere is fantastic—the sounds, the piano, the violin (I’m not well-versed in classical music, but it all feels incredibly authentic). 
+ The fear is masterfully directed. Absolutely brilliant.

Cons -: 
- Optimization. I’m getting 960 FPS in-game. You might think, “Wow, that’s great,” but it means the system is under near-full load. The game should have an FPS cap to prevent players’ rigs from catching fire. 🔥
- Sound balance. Sometimes the audio is way louder than it should be. Other times, you’re sitting in absolute silence. Feels a bit off.

Comments =: 
= I wasn’t a huge fan of how the menu is designed. It fits well with the game since a similar mechanic is used during gameplay, but it just felt inconvenient to me. Not bad enough to be a con, though.
= The game has criminally little marketing, but it deserves way more attention.
= Surprisingly detailed settings for an indie game—didn’t expect this many options!
= A bunch of languages available at launch, which is also a big plus.

Thanks for reading! ❤️

I cannot recommend One Deck Galaxy, due to a mixture of personal taste and general issue with the game.

There are, in escalating order, three critical issues I have with the game:


1) The game feels over-complicated, especially when it comes to the Adversaries.

Complexity isn't necessarily a bad thing - 4x titles like Stellaris or Endless Space thrive on interlocking systems that form the basis of their mechanics.

The problem is that One Deck Galaxy is not a 4x game; it is, in fact, a Rougelike that plays a bit like a cross between Dicey Dungeons and Renowned Explorers.  You roll dice, then use those dice to either trade for resources, explore and claim planets, or complete a check vs. the Adversary.  Each Adversary has a ludicrously convoluted way of determining what it will do during each turn, but in practice it all boils down to hoovering up resources the player needs, and then either locking them behind specific actions or banishing them from the game entirely.  The difference maker is that, in that convoluted process lies particulars that affect what you ought to be doing to play optimally.  It may take several attempts just to figure out what the hell you're meant to be doing.


2) The game feels over-tuned, to the point of being punitive and frustrating.

For some reason, the Adversaries' resource hoovering is at its worst at the very beginning of the game.  This means that you [b]have[/b] to Confront it at the earliest opportunity.  However, presumably in an effort to make the game harder, Confronting the Adversary is very frequently difficult to impossible without taking multiple turns to either get additional dice or get the required values on those dice.  As this is happening, the Adversary is both exiling cards from the deck and forcing you to pay additional costs.  Having to pay those costs means you have to devote resources to that instead of getting more dice or accumulating the resources required to Confront.  And while [i]that's[/i] happening, you're also not accumulating the resources required to raise your Federation Level, which you also need to do in order to Confront the Adversary again later.

Sometimes you get Encounter cards.  These things were clearly meant to be addressed after you've had a chance to Confront the Adversary, as they frequently require a level 2 starbase...  Except you can get them on turn 1.  You can get [i]multiple[/i] Encounters on turn one.  These further restrict your ability to act, meaning more turns wasted while the Adversary soft-locks you.


3) It just feels bad to play.

This is definitely the most down to personal taste, but it's also the biggest reason I actively dislike playing One Deck Galaxy.

I do not like the way the game aggressively kneecaps resource acquisition.  I do not like the way the Adversaries locked away dice until it became mathematically impossible to Confront them.  I do not like the way Federation levels all feel like acquiring them feels mutually exclusive with upgrading the Space Station, Confronting the Adversary, and acquiring Techs and Colonies - you need to do all three, but because of how all-or-nothing the systems are you inevitably end up losing time because you didn't do the other two, and oh look now you have to spend more resources and that threshold you were about to meet falls out of reach again.

This game doesn't leave me with the feeling that I made a mistake that I can learn from when I lose a run.  It leaves me feeling like I'm being asked to thread three needles with a single thread, only the needles are a mile apart and the thread is 3 inches long.

A fantastic SHMUP!

This one uses a shield mechanic; You need to hold on/off the shield button frequently to pass through bullets and lasers. The shield recharges quickly and It reflects the bullets back when you release the button (often incentivizing or forcing you to move into the bullets).

The game has some interesting scrolling level designs and well-made bosses with multiple phases that feel different from one another.  I played another game from the same dev recently: [b]Blade Chimera[/b] and it wouldn't surprise me if they used the same soundtrack for both of them (probably didn't, but it has that same, lively-but-filler vibe).

As is common in this genre, it's a little too short.  Which is my only real complaint with the game.  

This is why my favourite SHMUP is the survivor-roguelite hybrid: [b]Gunlocked[/b].  I think genre mashups of that nature will eventually be the future of SHMUPs (for me, at least).

[h2]Scores[/h2]
Graphics: 8/10. Really good for an indie EA game.

[b]Performance[/b]: 4/10. Runs poorly at the moment. Dev has promised to improve the performance via releases.

[b]Gameplay[/b]: 9/10. Roguelite & Industry Sim. YMMV. This is a niche genre, but fans on Hades/Binding of Isaac/etc and Factorio/DSP/Satisfactoru will love it for sure. Closest games in my opinion are either Hardspace:Shipbreakers or Mindustry.

[b]Length[/b]: Short at the moment. Can 0-100 the game as it is in about 5 hours on my 3rd playthrough. This is supposed to be about 30% of the game assuming difficulty doesn't scale, which it probably will.

[h2]Pros[/h2]
Great gameplay loop. Just one more asteroid is commonplace here. Balance is great at the moment for obstacles. Pirates show up later which seem to be a polarizing point for people in the playtest. I found them ignorable and easy. Some people found them very difficult.

Progression is great. You start out manually doing tasks on each asteroid which eventually get automated via workers & machines. New resource types show up with higher rewards and specific constraints (think like ETS2 hauling qualifications). Keeps it challenging.

Dev involvement: The devs are super active on Discord. Most stuff is replied to by one of the devs within 15 mins. They are very open to suggestions. They are also not afraid to not cater to every demand the playtesters make. If they continue on these lines, game will be a definite 9/10 on release date.

[h2]Cons[/h2]
EA: Game is in EA. Comes with all the normal EA caveats. Content quantity, balance and optimisation are lacking, which the devs are aware of and are improving on. There has been substantial change in the last 6 months. The game I started playtesting was much smaller and very barebones. 

If you're open to a bit of jank, I'd recommend this game 100%.

The game needs a lot of work. It has promise, but there are a lot of fundamental things that need to be addressed:

2) It is not a very "Automation" game. It is a time-limited node-hopper, where you quickly go and put down buildings, then gather them up at the end of (up to) 40 min runs. In truth, most you'll be doing is 20 minute runs.
3) Resource processing is constantly interrupted. Want to sleep? Go back and set all your processing up again on the ship you sleep on. Want to travel to a new node? Reset all your processing again. It's ridiculous.
4) Asteroid Classification =/= Size or Resource quantity. A (Class) CC-1 rock can have multiple ship loads of resources, or you can only get half a ship worth.... a CC-4 rock is a gamble too. There is no consistency. In my experience, the classification doesn't even relate to the resources it HAS on it. Higher class can 'roll' higher tier resources, but quantity and size of rock is always a gamble.

This is not an automation game! It feels like the first 15 minutes of playing Factorio, over and over again, with no "automation" tools, repeat from scratch on the next asteroid. This is a just game that does not respect your time.

- 90% of the game is spent mining by hand
- The entire automation aspect of the game needs to be significantly expanded. And no, placing down mining turrets does not count as automation, you still have to pick up all the ore yourself. You also can't prioritize materials to mine, they just mine the first thing they see.
- Procedural generation is very boring. There is only 1 asteroid "type" with different "color" variations and that's it. No caves, no crystals/structures/alien artifacts or distress beacons to find, nothing. Just randomly placed veins in the most annoying locations.
- Having to wait 30 seconds for a jump is absurd, especially when you have multiple jump cells. You have to wait for every single one of them: click, jump, wait 30 seconds, click another point, jump, wait 30 seconds again, repeat until you arrive at a desired asteroid.
[strike] - No market for refined minerals. You can only sell raw ore. Refined materials are only used for upgrades as far as I can tell. [/strike]
- Combat is janky. You cannot shoot up or down, like what? Good luck hitting anything when you're standing on a rock. You don't get an advance warning when pirates land, they just land instantly in a random spot on an asteroid, and can instantly destroy your expensive equipment while you're trying to find where they are. They don't drop loot, so this whole "pirates" mechanic just removes fun from the gameplay.
- The whole "shuttle navigation" minigame of not trying to hit an asterioid is annoying. It purely exists to add grind when going from A to B. There is no value to be gained here, needs to be significantly reworked or removed.
- Ship/station management could have just been a menu. There is no reason for your physical character to go to a fuel station, hit E, then click Buy Fuel, then repeat with the other stations. It could have just been a tab in the UI, like a market tab, fuel tab, upgrades tab, etc. Having to physically walk just adds grind to the game, and masks the severe lack of content.
- A lot of micro-bugs which detract from the experience. No major issues, but so many little bugs that add up and make the game unfun.
- Sound design needs some work. A lot of harsh and unpleasant sounds with no way to mute them without muting the game.
- Music is just... bad. For such a repetitive game, having repetitive music is a death sentence.

I think it would be a lot more fun if you managed multiple asteroid "bases" at the same time. Hop on an asteroid, place down equipment, warp to the next one, then come back and grab the loot.

Conclusion - this is about a $6 game in terms of the current state. Play ΔV: Rings of Saturn for a more finished space mining game.

I will preface this by saying that if you are already somewhat interested in this game, and it's on offer, then for how little it costs, I can easily recommend picking it up. There’s enough content in the game that will be worth the price of admission, and there’s even a demo; again, if you played it and it’s got you interested, you will find it worth the price.
 
As for the game itself, I think it's rather quite good. There’s quite a lot this game does right as an indie title, though there are also some issues and problems that are present. Note: this review will be as spoiler-free as possible.
 
The gameplay is a story-driven platformer with elements of stealth, action and a little bit of puzzling. You control a dog called Bea who starts off living on Earth before being separated from their adoptive owner. They then end up embarking (pun intended) on a quest to reunite themselves while exploring the depths of space. In terms of the gameplay, it is a classic 2.5D platformer and all the staples are accounted for and familiar. You have three innate “senses” which you can use to aid you: hearing, which allows you to visually see sounds; smell, which allows you to see which gases are poisonous and what scent you have for some puzzles; and sight, which allows you to see connections between things like buttons and doors. The game makes good use of these, and they are very useful if you want to find additional collectables and hidden lore. Another notable mechanic is the ability to communicate with the various inhabitants that you come across in the story. I find this mechanic just “ok”. It’s not anything particularly special, and the only punishment for messing it up is having to wait or dodge away while the creature returns to their neutral state. My main issue is there is no depth to it; simply choose a starting action, see how they react and go from there. Where the problem lies is that if you pair each action with their counterpart on the opposite side of the radial menu, they cancel each other out. This means you cannot ever lose any encounter – simply choose an action, if it didn’t move the creature to a happy state, simply perform the opposite action and try another action.
 
The story is perhaps the next big piece and very much drives the gameplay. I will not spoil anything here, but I found the story to be, in contrast to the communication system, much more fleshed out and with quite a bit of depth to it. There are loads of characters, artefacts and lots of general information that does a fantastic job at describing the fictional universe. While traversing levels, you can find areas, which you can scan to get lore fragments. These can be read in the menu and, to my surprise, have a decent amount of information in each of them. These are actually quite fun to read, and it really does complement the story – aside from one bit, which I’ll get to later. A couple of minor issues I do have is that it firstly can be described in a single word: “contrived”. To me, it feel like the next stage in the game was heavily forced by the cutscene that preceded it. The issue is, after you finish the stages on a planet, it feels like you could just go straight to the end of the game from a narrative point of view. The cutscenes’ remedy to this is by having a significant amount happen in about 4 panels of narrated images. The whole set of stages on a planet could take an hour where, typically, you have one or two goals that progress the story. Then, the cutscene happens and loads of things happen, and you’re now on a new planet. It could just be me, but the story felt a little disjointed – more like every planet had its own story written in isolation, and then the overarching story tried to link them together.
 
The final bit of the game requires you to make two choices; both affect the story, and one of them affects the final gameplay. A small thing with this is one of the choices makes absolutely no sense in my opinion. One of the choices is between destroying two entities, or combining them. Throughout the whole game, each of these entities has been described, documented and shown to be chaotic and evil – which makes the choice of unifying or destroying them seem a non-choice; clearly the latter is what should be done. Strangely, if you download and complete the two DLC levels, you will be given two cutscenes which explains these entities, how they were created and what they stand for, which makes this choice actually a meaningful choice. If these pieces of information were present to the player before the decision, then this would seem like a simple fix.
 
As for the soundtrack, I’m someone who enjoys game soundtracks and plays them more than regular songs. I’m happy to say this one is quite a nice addition to my collection. It’s more focused around ambient/atmospheric pieces, and it does the job very well. Soundtracks are always the most subjective, but for me this was a decent OST.
 
The art style is also nothing short of fantastic. It’s very well constructed in my opinion and there are a number of places in the game that look amazing, despite not having an advanced lighting system in the game engine or anything like that. This extends to the cutscenes as well which, while they are basically just still images with a little bit of animation, again the art style really shines.
 
So far, my review has been based on my casual playthrough. At this point, I would say this is a good game, close to being great even. Unfortunately, where this game is at its worst is when going for completion.
 
I wanted to go back and collect all the lore fragments, and find all the hidden skins you can get for Bea...at which point I found some infuriating bugs. While I did encounter some bugs on my initial playthrough, they weren’t frequent – the same cannot be said when going for completion. There are lots of minor bugs: Bea freaking out when on the edge of ledges; some abilities and senses not activating; the gravity of objects getting very confused when you jump; all fine examples. Where the game became infuriating was the collision detection...or lack thereof. For some reason, collisions will just refuse to detect anything sometimes. I will sit on collectables and they won’t be collected, buttons won’t be pressed, etc. It is much more prevalent because the game seems to recalculate collisions whenever you die – which you will do a lot of when trying to find collectables. When I load into a level, the collision can be fine but then I die and can no longer hit a button I could previously. You can die again to hopefully fix it...except that can sometimes mean losing a huge amount of progress for levels that have few checkpoints. And when I say collision detection, while I’ve yet to fall through the floor, the triggers that take you to the next stage can also fail to register – the closest I got to quitting the game out of frustration was a little over halfway into the story where I died jumping into a pit. I naturally assumed that it meant it was a bottomless pit I should avoid. I then spent at least 20 minutes trying to find a way to progress because the only thing that I could do was move left...but be blocked by a box that I could never jump high enough over, or jump to the right...which was blocked by electric gates. There was literally nothing else I could think of and so after racking my brains I decided to try the pit again and...it loaded the next stage. Extremely frustrating.
 
The only good thing I can say about completion is that the achievements do not seem to be adjusted for the DLC levels, meaning you actually only need 29/31 lore fragments and 18/20 skins to get them.
 
I do want to end this by saying I did overall enjoy my time playing it, and I definitely got more than my money's worth from it. As this is the first game by this indie studio, I cannot expect it to be flawless and I will say, even with the bugs, this is a good attempt at a first game.

[h1]My Furry Maid 🐾: A Paw-some Adventure with Flaws Worth Debating[/h1]

[b]Author:[/b] Kiba Snowpaw, Alpha Male Ice Wolf of HowlStrom  
[b]Developer & Publisher:[/b] Dirty Fox Games   
[b]Perspective:[/b] From an Ice Mage who’s been through countless blizzards (and visual novels), let’s explore this steamy, heartwarming slice-of-life!  

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Introduction[/h2]  
My Furry Maid 🐾 is yet another addition to the "My Furry" universe, developed by Dirty Fox Games. Released on November 19, 2022, it is a short visual novel with a Match-3 gameplay twist and a story-driven approach that revolves around relationships, humor, and drama. While it has charm and warmth to spare, there are notable elements that both elevate and hold it back from being an anthro masterpiece.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Basic Plot Summary[/h2]  
The story follows a teacher at a housekeeping school who takes on a new student named Anna. She’s an aspiring actress seeking to perfect her maid skills for an upcoming role. As the week progresses, you guide Anna through etiquette, cleaning, and cooking, with plenty of wholesome moments and budding romance. Will you both stay professional, or will deeper feelings blossom? This kinetic visual novel is simple but effective in crafting an intimate atmosphere.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Originality[/h2]  
Though visual novels are a dime a dozen in the indie scene, My Furry Maid shines with its niche focus on the maid trope combined with anthro appeal. While the premise of a “teacher-student” dynamic is common, the light-hearted tone and occasional serious topics (like self-discovery and chasing dreams) give it a personality. However, this formula feels repetitive across the series, which might make returning players feel a sense of déjà vu.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]The Studio Behind the Magic[/h2]  
Dirty Fox Games has become a staple in the furry VN space, delivering games like [i]My Furry Stepmom[/i] and [i]My Dragon Party[/i]. Known for their attention to character design and “slice-of-life” storytelling, they focus on creating quick, digestible experiences with relatable characters. Compared to more narrative-driven VNs like [i]Nekopara[/i], Dirty Fox Games caters to a niche audience that craves a blend of fluff and mild spice.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Analysis and Evaluation[/h2]  

[u]Gameplay Mechanics:[/u]  
The Match-3 mechanic is functional but feels tacked on. While it offers light interactivity, it doesn’t evolve much, and players might breeze through without much challenge. However, it does act as a breather between the story segments.  

[u]Visuals and Art Design:[/u]  
Anna’s design is undeniably the highlight—she’s cute, expressive, and feels alive in every scene. The art is clean, with high-quality sprites and polished backgrounds. That said, the environments can feel static and lack detail, especially compared to more immersive visual novels.  

[u]Writing and Humor:[/u]  
The dialogue is snappy and endearing, often leaning into wholesome humor. However, the pacing can feel rushed, especially as the story barrels toward its conclusion. For a game trying to balance romance and drama, a longer runtime would have allowed more room for emotional payoffs.  

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Character Development[/h2]  

[b]Anna:[/b]  
As the central character, Anna is a well-written, lovable protagonist with a mix of naivety and determination. Her growth, from clumsy newbie to confident actress, is heartwarming, though the short runtime means some arcs feel underexplored.  

[b]Supporting Cast:[/b]  
There isn’t much depth beyond Anna and the main character. While their interactions are charming, other characters, like students or faculty, could’ve added more layers to the story.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Structure[/h2]  
The game runs for about 1.5 hours, making it one of the shorter entries in the "My Furry" lineup. While it works as a bite-sized experience, its brevity is a double-edged sword, as some moments feel rushed, and the world-building takes a backseat.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Sound and Music[/h2]  
The soundtrack does its job, offering relaxing background tunes that fit the cozy maid-school vibe. However, it’s not particularly memorable. Voice acting is absent, which might disappoint those seeking a more immersive experience.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Performance and Technical Aspects[/h2]  
[b]Stability:[/b] The game runs flawlessly on most systems, and its lightweight nature ensures smooth performance.  
[b]Accessibility:[/b] Options for text speed and screen adjustments make it user-friendly, but a lack of language variety limits its audience.  

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Impact and Legacy[/h2]  
While My Furry Maid doesn’t reinvent the genre, it’s a solid addition to Dirty Fox’s portfolio. Its strength lies in appealing to fans of anthro-themed romance, and it’s a fun, albeit brief, romp for newcomers. Longtime players, however, might find the series’ repetitive nature starting to wear thin.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Praise and Critique[/h2]  

[b]Strengths:[/b]  
[list]  
[*]Anna’s delightful character design and personality.  
[*]Polished, high-quality art assets.  
[*]Light-hearted tone with occasional depth.  
[*]Great entry point for newcomers to the series.  
[/list]  

[b]Weaknesses:[/b]  
[list]  
[*]Extremely short runtime limits character development.  
[*]Repetitive formula across the series.  
[*]Underwhelming Match-3 mechanics.  
[*]Static, uninspired backgrounds.  
[/list]  

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Comparison[/h2]  
Compared to furry VNs like [i]Nekopara[/i] or [i]Winds of Change[/i], My Furry Maid feels more casual and less ambitious. While it excels in charm, it doesn’t push boundaries or offer the narrative depth seen in its contemporaries. Fans of Dirty Fox Games’ other titles will likely enjoy it, but those seeking innovation might be left wanting.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Conclusion[/h2]  
My Furry Maid 🐾 is a cozy, charming visual novel that plays it safe. Its strengths lie in its art and character interactions, but it falls short of its potential due to its short runtime and lack of depth. For furry fans looking for a light-hearted escape, it’s worth the price of admission, but don’t expect it to revolutionize the genre.

[b]Final Rating:[/b] 7/10 - Cute, but not groundbreaking.

So, it might seem weird how the Prologue had thumbs up but this one doesn't. Yet again we meet with the problem of Steam not allowing neutral reviews.
I cannot in good conscience say that Glorious Princess was a good sequel. It felt inferior in many aspects to it's own predecessor.

The story felt naive. The reuse of content in the form of flashbacks to things you have seen literally thirty minutes to an hour prior is insane padding making up at least 15% of the game. The writing somehow felt worse than the last time (and it's crazy how I say "last time" when I've beaten the Prologue literally two days prior to leaving this review). "Good is good and bad is bad except when good does bad things then it's no longer good or something" is what this game's story comes across as. And that's not even comparing it to the power struggle and (predictable) subversion of expectations of its' own prequel. It's just bad as a standalone, and simply disappointing as a second chapter. I do appreciate the fact there's a greater story behind separate entries with a bit of a gray morale in it but I can't help but wish it wasn't presented in the way Glorious Princess did.

The fights are padding as well. You fight the same group of enemies placed five times in a row, fight a different group of enemies placed three times next to each other, fight a mix of the two copypasted a couple times... It feels nice the first, maybe the second time to have to make up a specific tactic to use against specific enemy encounter. It doesn't feel so good to repeat that over and over again THAT many times. I got bored just before the final area and just walked past all the enemies when I saw there are about twenty encounters which aren't even worth wasting time on. The final boss felt good though. Maybe a couple mid-bosses weren't so bad either. I just can't remember, the aftertaste of all the minor fights is too overpowering.

The maps are... I don't think I can stress enough how bland they were. Even the generic dungeons of Prologue felt better. There are even two situations where two screens are pretty much entirely reused (and no, that's not including the "base").

Overall I can't recommend it even to people who have played the Hero King Quest. It's not terrible, but...
I, personally, am keeping an eye on and waiting for the Bloody Emperor, but I only hope it doesn't turn out to be such a letdown. Peacemaker series could be better but I hope this entry is just a minor hiccup before a good triquel.

The game suffers from quite a bit of jank. It is possible to lodge yourself into floaty places, and the way the protagonist grabs after holds can be weird at certain angles. The tools at your disposal are also very powerful, so you can with a little effort and intent, easily go places you are not meant to and clip through the rock. Performance also isn't great, but maybe that's just because my 1060 is gettting old. 

Overall I can really reccomend this game if you enjoy scenic, atmospheric games and are looking to delve into an interesting world for a little bit, if you would like to try a unique and fun take on movement puzzles and can forgive the occasional rough edges in a game with clear love and imagination put behind it.

A short yet enthralling game with a relaxed pace and charming art style, not to mention a wonderful soundtrack. Jusant is more about atmosphere than anything else, and it does a decent job of conveying that throughout its various chapters.

Though mechanically and thematically different, there is an interesting similarity it shares with 'Outer Wilds', in that the player is retracing the steps of people who existed before their time, and this is done through reading notes and logs about their lives and endeavours. The tone shifts from fun, to nostalgic, to sombre, to outright sad; but overall, there is a pervasive sense of solitude that underscores everything, and it gives the game a unique feeling which I found quite engaging.

The full price is a bit steep for the overall duration, but with a discount it is definitely worth a look if you're into casually paced games with no real stakes and a focus on atmosphere.

NOTE: Though I'm not going to let it affect my positive review, it is worth mentioning that the performance of this game can be inconsistent at times, which isn't entirely unusual for Unreal Engine games. There were moments where the least demanding environments would tank my FPS to sub-60 for no apparent reason, but my hardware is quite old, so take that with a grain of salt.

Yeah, hate to do this, Dontnod, but this one isn't it, have to be honest.

I was honestly on a fence in terms of whether to mark this as a poisitive or negative and if steam offered a neutral, I would definitely go for that.

The positive is definitely the music and the atmosphere. I am honestly still, despite my negative review, likely going to get a vinyl of this soundtrack. It's a great combination of mysterious fantasy and cuteness all at once. Especially at first half it felt so interesting to go through the ruins of previously clearly breathing and living place and getting fragments of what it used to be both through letters & through the seashells. At the first half and a change, I was still pretty sure I will recommend this despite the shortcomings.

The negatives was the controls, or overall gameplay itself. It felt so clunky at times and jumps that I was sure I am going to make based on my past experience I suddenly couldn't do the next time. It became even more obvious to me that the controls, albeit original, are not really that intuitive, when I came back to the game after a short pause and it felt clunky once again. Furthermore, so many times it seemed like when I progressed, it felt like I skipped over something and that in no way was that supposed to be a way forward that was intended to be taken. A lot of times I also arrived at a location having no clue where the f to go next - luckily figured out later that if I just save and open the menu, I will be conveniently shown which way to face now. There is a mechanic where you can see where to go next, but from my experience it was showing such random things that it might have as well said "Go up, you are climbing, remember?" every time.

So my make or break ended up being "this is intruiging, let's see where the story goes. Who am I? Why am I here? What ended up happening to everyone?" - and that... Was not a satisfying ending in that regard. The whole game is more of an atmospheric trip than something that I would dare describe as coherent. So although it is clearly labour of love, I myself lean to the negative, rather than a positive. But I do appreciate the obvious attempt at creating something new and original - that I applaud. 

Go give it a try yourself though. For me it was like a movie that I did not end up enjoying fully, but which parts I appreciate experiencing.

This game is worth every penny. I'm always hunting for Castlevania clones and Indiemania really does well putting its own spin on the formula.

There's little as rewarding as beating a tough boss battle and being duly rewarded with images of their head being ripped open and brains splattering all over.

So much is going on under the hood here, and it's all about the little touches. This probably has my favorite implementation of the Sonic-style underwater air bubble mechanic. Occasionally there's fun sections where you're able to use an item/creature that grants unique powers, like turning into a giant frog or a plant helicopter. The levels are expansive and encourage a little bit of exploration and there's so much enemy variety between stages.

I would feel no shame buying such a fully featured game at full price. Please make more!
